definition_zh: 深渊；深不可测的空间；巨大鸿沟
definition_en: a very deep hole or space that seems to have no bottom, or a huge difference between two things
core_image: 向下望不见底的黑洞：光沉下去就消失了
scene: 他站在崖边俯瞰，脚下云雾翻涌，怎么也望不到底。He felt he was staring into an abyss.
sceneCN: 这里 abyss 是「深渊」（第 1 个义项：深不见底的空间）；句意为他感觉自己正凝视深渊。

collocations.phrase: the abyss between rich and poor

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「深不可测的」，今多指「极差的」
由 abysmal 加副词后缀构成，义为「极其糟糕地」

senses.title: A bottomless deep space
senses.definition: a very deep hole in the ground or in the ocean that seems endless
senses.definitionCN: 地面或海洋中深得似乎没有底的洞
senses.example: The divers explored an abyss beneath the ice shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员探测了冰架下方的深渊。
senses.why: The Greek root meant bottomless, so the first image is simply a depth with no floor to stop the fall.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根本义为「无底的」，所以第一个意象就是一段没有底可以停住坠落的深度。

senses.title: A gap between two things
senses.definition: a very large difference or division between two groups or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 两个群体或观念之间极大的差别或隔阂
senses.example: There is a vast abyss between the two negotiating positions.
senses.exampleCN: 两方谈判立场之间存在巨大鸿沟。
senses.why: If a bottomless pit separates two cliffs, no bridge can cross it; that picture was borrowed for abstract differences.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个无底深坑隔开两座悬崖，任何桥都无法跨越；这个画面被借来形容抽象的巨大差异。

senses.title: Emotional or mental ruin
senses.definition: a state of deep sadness, despair, or moral collapse
senses.definitionCN: 深深的悲伤、绝望或道德崩塌的状态
senses.example: After losing everything, he sank into an abyss of despair.
senses.exampleCN: 失去一切之后，他坠入了绝望的深渊。
senses.why: Falling has always stood for losing control, so a bottomless fall becomes the picture of utter hopelessness.
senses.whyCN: 坠落历来象征失控，于是无底的坠落成为彻底绝望的写照。

intro.en: Abyss comes through Latin abyssus from Greek abussos, 'bottomless', built on a- 'without' and bussos 'depth'.
intro.cn: abyss 经拉丁语 abyssus 来自希腊语 abussos（无底的），由表示「无」的前缀与「深处」词根构成。

items.en: The root *dheu- suggested deep, dark places, feeding Greek bussos.
items.cn: 词根一般认为与「深的、暗的处所」相关，成为希腊语 bussos 的来源。

items.en: abussos combined a- 'without' with bussos 'bottom, depth' to mean bottomless.
items.cn: abussos 由表示否定的前缀加 bussos（底、深处）构成，意为无底。

items.en: In ancient Greek texts the word named the fathomless pit beneath the world.
items.cn: 在古希腊文本中，该词指世界之下深不可测的坑洞。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek form as abyssus.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语形式借为 abyssus。

items.en: Old French turned it into abisme, later abysme.
items.cn: 古法语将其变为 abisme，后又作 abysme。

items.en: English adopted the form abyss, keeping both the literal and figurative depths.
items.cn: 英语采纳 abyss 一形，同时保留字面与比喻两种深度。

note.en: The first group gathers the word family from the same Greek root; the second gathers words for deep hollows.
note.cn: 第一组收同一希腊词根的词族；第二组收表示深坑深谷的词。

entries.definition: Adjective from the same root; now usually meaning extremely bad.
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，今多指「极差的」。

entries.definition: Adverb of abysmal, meaning to a very bad degree.
entries.definitionCN: abysmal 的副词，义为「糟糕透顶地」。

entries.definition: Adjective describing the deep zones of the ocean.
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，描述深海深层的。

entries.definition: A deep crack in the earth or a sharp difference between people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「裂口；巨大分歧」。

entries.definition: A wide gap, often between opinions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海湾；（观点间的）鸿沟」。

entries.definition: A completely empty space.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「空虚；空旷的空间」。

entries.definition: A deep narrow valley cut by water.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「深谷；沟壑」，有形可见，非无底。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'no bottom' Greek root and the ocean scenes; the abstract hooks picture the fall itself.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用希腊语「无底」词根与海洋场景；抽象记忆点想象坠落本身。

normal.en: A- in Greek means without; bussos means depth.
normal.cn: 希腊语前缀 a- 表示「无」，bussos 表示「深处」。

normal.en: So an abyss is literally 'no depth', a place with no bottom.
normal.cn: 所以 abyss 字面是「无底」，一个没有底的所在。

normal.en: Oceanographers use abyssal zones for the deepest seas.
normal.cn: 海洋学家用 abyssal zones 指最深的海域。

normal.en: The plural is abysses, double s kept in the middle.
normal.cn: 复数为 abysses，中间的双 s 保留。

normal.en: The adjective abysmal drifted to mean terrible.
normal.cn: 形容词 abysmal 逐渐漂移为「极差的」。

abstract.en: Picture a black hole in the ground where dropped stones never sound.
abstract.cn: 想象地上一个黑洞，扔下的石头永远听不到回响。

abstract.en: Picture two cliffs so far apart that no bridge reaches.
abstract.cn: 想象两座相隔极远的悬崖，任何桥都够不着。

abstract.en: Picture a person falling and never seeing a floor below.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人不断坠落，脚下永远不见地面。

examples.en: The submarine descended toward the abyss of the trench.
examples.cn: 潜艇向海沟深处下潜。

examples.en: Between the two cultures lies an abyss of misunderstanding.
examples.cn: 两种文化之间横亘着误解的鸿沟。

examples.en: She gazed into the abyss and felt both fear and wonder.
examples.cn: 她凝视深渊，既感到恐惧也感到惊叹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿逼死」——洞深得望不到底，望久了让人心里发慌，仿佛要被黑暗吞掉。

root: 希腊语 a-（无）+ bussos（底、深处）→ abussos（无底的）；核心义是「没有底的深处」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a literal bottomless depth, to a metaphorical gap, to a state of despair.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从字面的无底深渊，走向比喻的巨大鸿沟，再走向绝望的境地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a depth with no bottom where light disappears
core.cn: 核心意象：不见底的深度，光沉下去就消失

branches.en: The literal deep hole in earth or ocean.
branches.cn: 大地或海洋中字面上的深洞。

branches.en: The width of the hole becomes the distance between groups.
branches.cn: 洞的宽度变成群体之间的距离。

branches.en: The endless fall becomes a life of hopelessness.
branches.cn: 无尽的坠落变成无望的人生。

branches.en: Differences so wide that no argument can bridge them.
branches.cn: 大到任何论证都无法跨越的分歧。

branches.en: Both senses share the feeling of something one cannot climb out of.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享「无法爬出」的感受。

intro.en: The word is a Greek negative prefix on a depth stem; its family adds adjectives and an adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语否定前缀加「深处」词干构成，词族另派生形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin abyssus is the direct borrowing of the Greek form, so the Latin entry records the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abyssus 是希腊形式的直接借词，拉丁条目记录该名词。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「深不可测的；极差的」
副词，义为「极其糟糕地」
形容词，义为「深渊的；深海层的」

definition_zh: 学术的；学业的；纯理论的；学院派的；普通学科的；以学术见长的；大学教师、学者
definition_en: relating to study, research and teaching at a university, or existing only in theory rather than in practice
core_image: 深夜图书馆的一张桌子，一摞书、一支笔和一盏不肯关的台灯
scene: 开学第一周，宿舍楼下的公告栏贴满了课程和考试安排。The academic year begins in early September.
sceneCN: 这里的 academic 是「学业的、学校的」（第 2 个义项：与学校学习安排有关）；句意为学年在九月初开始。画面里有公告栏、课程表和刚返校的学生。

pos.zh: 形容词：学术的；学业的；纯理论的；学院派的

collocations.zh: 纯理论的；与实际无关的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「学业上；学术上」
同源名词，义为「学院；研究院；专科学校」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「院士；学会会员」
同源名词，义为「学术界；学术圈」

senses.title: Relating to scholarly research
senses.definition: connected with serious study and research, especially at a university
senses.definitionCN: 与严肃的学习和研究有关，尤指大学里的研究
senses.example: Her academic research focuses on how children learn to read.
senses.exampleCN: 她的学术研究关注儿童如何学会阅读。
senses.why: The word starts from the name of the grove where Plato taught, so its first job is to mark whatever belongs to that world of study.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是柏拉图授课那片园子的名字，所以它最本职的工作就是标示「属于那个研究世界」的东西。

senses.title: Relating to school study and results
senses.titleCN: 学业的：与在校学习有关
senses.definition: connected with study, lessons and results at a school or college rather than with sport or social life
senses.definitionCN: 与学校或学院的课程、学习和成绩有关，而非体育或社交生活
senses.example: The academic year begins in early September.
senses.exampleCN: 学年在九月初开始。
senses.why: Once the word belongs to the school, it naturally covers the calendar and the marks of school life, not only research in a library.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词属于学校，它自然就覆盖了学校生活里的日历与分数，而不只是图书馆里的研究。

senses.title: Only true in theory, not in practice
senses.definition: of a question or argument, having no practical effect because the real decision has already been made
senses.definitionCN: 指问题或争论没有实际影响，因为真正的决定早已作出
senses.example: Whether the rule is fair is academic now that the contract is signed.
senses.exampleCN: 合同都签了，这条规则公不公平已经只是理论问题。
senses.why: What lives only in books has no weight in the street; a question with no practical consequence is confined to the study.
senses.whyCN: 只活在书里的东西在街上没有分量；一个不产生实际后果的问题，就被关进了书房。

senses.title: Dry and bookish in style
senses.titleCN: 学院派的：拘泥书本、脱离实际
senses.definition: of writing, art or thinking, correct but dry, showing more study than life
senses.definitionCN: 指写作、艺术或思想正确却干枯，书卷气多于生活感
senses.example: The film was praised abroad but called academic at home.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片在国外受好评，在本国却被说成学院派。
senses.why: The same belonging to the study becomes a criticism when the study is cut off from the street: too much book, too little life.
senses.whyCN: 同样一种「属于书房」的属性，一旦书房与街道隔绝，就变成批评：书太多，生活太少。

senses.title: A university teacher or researcher
senses.definition: a person who teaches or does research at a university, used as a countable noun
senses.definitionCN: 在大学任教或做研究的人，作可数名词使用
senses.example: She is a young academic with two books to her name.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位年轻学者，已经出过两本书。
senses.why: From the adjective describing the world of study, English made a noun for a person who lives in that world.
senses.whyCN: 从描述「研究世界」的形容词出发，英语造出一个名词，专指生活在这个世界里的人。

senses.title: Of caps, gowns and ceremonies
senses.definition: relating to the traditional dress and ceremonies of universities, such as gowns and caps
senses.definitionCN: 与大学的传统服饰和仪式有关，如学位袍和学位帽
senses.example: The graduates posed for photos in full academic dress.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业生们穿着全套学位服拍照。
senses.why: The oldest sense of belonging to a place of learning survives most visibly in its costume, where the tradition is worn on the body.
senses.whyCN: 「属于学府」这一最古老的含义，最显眼地保存在服装上：传统被穿在了身上。

senses.title: Of subjects taught for their own sake
senses.definition: of school subjects such as history or physics, studied for knowledge rather than for a trade
senses.definitionCN: 指历史、物理这类以求知为目的、而非为职业训练设置的学科
senses.example: The school offers a strong academic curriculum alongside its sports program.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校除了体育项目，还提供扎实的学科课程。
senses.why: If a subject belongs to the world of study rather than to a workshop, it is called academic, and the word then labels a whole curriculum.
senses.whyCN: 一门科目如果属于研究的世界而不属于车间，就被称为 academic；这个词于是用来标示整类课程。

senses.title: Devoted to learning, of a person or family
senses.titleCN: 以读书治学见长的（人、家庭）
senses.definition: of a person, family or institution, valuing books, study and scholarship above practical or sporting success
senses.definitionCN: 指人、家庭或机构重视读书治学，胜过实际事务或体育成绩
senses.example: She grew up in an academic family where dinner talk was about books.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一个书香家庭长大，饭桌上的话题总是书。
senses.why: When a whole household is oriented toward study, the adjective stops describing a topic and starts describing a way of life.
senses.whyCN: 当一个家庭整体朝向读书治学，这个形容词就不再描述某个话题，而开始描述一种生活方式。

intro.en: Academic goes back to the name of the grove outside Athens where Plato taught, and from there to every school.
intro.cn: academic 可追到雅典城外柏拉图授课的那片园子的名字，再从那里走向一切学校。

items.en: Akademeia was the name of a grove and gymnasium near Athens, associated with the hero Akademos. The origin of the name itself is uncertain.
items.cn: Akademeia 是雅典附近一片园林与体育场的名字，与英雄 Akademos 有关；这个名称本身的来源不确定。

items.en: Akademikos meant 'of the Academy', the school Plato founded there; it described members and teachings of that circle.
items.cn: Akademikos 意为「学园的」，即柏拉图在此创办的学派；它形容该学派的成员与学说。

items.en: Latin academia named both the place and the philosophical school, and kept the word alive through learned writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 academia 既指那个地方，也指那个哲学学派，并通过学术写作把词保存了下来。

items.en: English borrowed academy in the sixteenth century, and academic followed as the adjective for things belonging to it.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 academy，随后 academic 作为「属于它的」形容词出现。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective also became a noun for a university teacher, and gained its mildly critical sense of 'out of touch'.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个形容词又变成指大学教师的名词，并获得「脱离实际」这一略带批评的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Greek name behind the word; the near-meaning group holds words about study, theory and teaching.
note.cn: 形近组共享这个词背后的希腊名称；近义组收与学习、理论、教学有关的词。

entries.definition: A school or society for a special field, such as an art or military academy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学院、研究院、专科学校」，如艺术学院或军校。

entries.definition: The world of universities and research, taken as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学术界、学术圈」，指大学与研究构成的整体世界。

entries.definition: A member of a learned academy or society.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「院士、学会会员」，指学术团体或学会的成员。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning in terms of study or school results.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「学业上、学术上」，用于说明在学习或成绩方面。

entries.definition: Showing careful study and deep knowledge; describes a person or a piece of work.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有学者风范的、学术性的」，多形容人或著作严谨有学问。

entries.definition: Relating to teaching and learning, often with the aim of helping people learn.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「教育的、有教育意义的」，范围比 academic 更宽。

entries.definition: Based on ideas rather than practice; closest to the 'purely academic' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「理论的」，与 academic 的「纯理论」一义最接近，但完全不涉及学校。

entries.definition: Relating to schools or to the medieval method of academic debate; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「学校的、经院式的」，语气正式，常用于中世纪学术辩论的语境。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek place name behind the word and the collocations it really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词背后的希腊地名，以及它真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: Akademeia was the grove where Plato taught: academic means belonging to that world of study.
normal.cn: Akademeia 是柏拉图授课的那片园子：academic 就是「属于那个研究世界」。

normal.en: academy is the place, academic is the adjective, academia is the whole world of it.
normal.cn: academy 是那个场所，academic 是形容词，academia 是整个学术圈。

normal.en: academic year is the school calendar, a fixed phrase worth learning whole.
normal.cn: academic year 指学年，是值得整体记住的固定说法。

normal.en: academic performance is the standard phrase for marks and results at school.
normal.cn: academic performance 是表示在校成绩的标准说法。

normal.en: purely academic means it only matters in theory, as in a purely academic question.
normal.cn: purely academic 表示只在理论上重要，例如纯理论的问题。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp still on in an empty library: someone is awake because a question is not finished.
abstract.cn: 想象空图书馆里还亮着一盏灯：有人醒着，因为一个问题还没想完。

abstract.en: The same word praises and mocks: it praises depth of study and mocks distance from life.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能赞美也能嘲讽：赞美钻研的深度，也嘲讽与生活的距离。

abstract.en: A grove became a school, a school became a university, and a university became a way of life.
abstract.cn: 一片园子变成一所学校，一所学校变成一所大学，一所大学又变成一种生活方式。

examples.en: He left his job to pursue an academic career in biology.
examples.cn: 他辞掉工作，去追求生物学方面的学术生涯。

examples.en: Her academic performance improved a lot after she changed schools.
examples.cn: 转学之后，她的学业成绩提高了很多。

examples.en: Whether the delay was legal is now an academic question.
examples.cn: 这次延期是否合法，如今已只是个理论问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卡德米」——阿卡德米的书房里堆满书，讲的是学术与学业。

root: 希腊语 Akadēmeia「雅典城外的学园」，相传与英雄 Akademos 有关，名称本身的来源不确定；柏拉图在此办学，遂有 Akadēmikos「学园的」，经拉丁语 academia 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Academic begins with one place of study and spreads outward: to research, to school results, to pure theory, to a dry style, to the people, the gowns, the subjects and the families of that world.
sensesIntro.cn: academic 从一处读书的地方开始向外扩散：学术研究、学校成绩、纯理论、干枯风格，以及那个世界里的人、礼服、学科与家庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp burning late over a desk of books inside a place of study.
core.cn: 核心意象：学府里一张书桌，灯亮到很晚。

branches.en: THE RESEARCH: whatever belongs to serious study and publication.
branches.cn: 研究线：属于严肃学习与发表的东西。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: the calendar, the marks and the subjects taught there.
branches.cn: 学校线：学年安排、成绩以及在校所教的科目。

branches.en: THE STUDY CUT OFF: what has no practical effect, or has too much book and too little life.
branches.cn: 书房隔绝线：不产生实际后果的东西，或书太多、生活太少的东西。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE AND DRESS: the teachers, and the gowns that make the tradition visible.
branches.cn: 人与服饰线：大学教师，以及让传统看得见的学位服。

branches.en: THE HOUSEHOLD: a whole family oriented toward books and learning.
branches.cn: 家庭线：整个家庭以读书治学为中心。

intro.en: Academic is a Greek place name turned adjective, and its family keeps the shape of the original school.
intro.cn: academic 是由希腊地名转成的形容词，其词族保留着那所学园最初的形状。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form academia carried the Greek word into European learning; the Greek name itself is the oldest recorded layer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 academia 把这个希腊词带进欧洲的学术传统；希腊语名称本身是最早有记录的层次。

items.example: The name belongs to a place, not to a root meaning study.
items.exampleCN: 这个名字属于一个地点，而不是一个意为「学习」的词根。

items.example: The adjective first described Plato's followers.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词最初描述柏拉图的追随者。

items.example: Latin kept the word alive in learned writing.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语在学术写作中把这个词保存下来。

items.example: The academy opened in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这所学院在十六世纪开办。
它由 academy 构成 academic。

items.example: The stem carries the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载着整个词族。

definition_zh: 学会会员；院士；学者
definition_en: a member of an academy, especially one that promotes art or science
core_image: 院士证：被正式选入最高学术殿堂的人
scene: 典礼上，白发老人从院长手中接过证书，正式成为科学院的一员。The new academician thanked the academy in his speech.
sceneCN: 这里 academician 是「院士、学会会员」（第 1 个义项：被选入学会的正式成员）；句意为新院士在致辞中感谢科学院。

collocations.phrase: an academician of the academy of sciences

derivatives.zh: 本词的基础名词，义为「学会；学院；研究院」
由 academy 派生的形容词，义为「学术的；学院的」
由 academic 加副词后缀构成，义为「在学术上」

senses.title: A member of an academy
senses.definition: a person formally elected to membership in an academy of arts or sciences
senses.definitionCN: 被正式选入艺术或科学学会的成员
senses.example: She was elected an academician at forty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 她四十五岁时当选为院士。
senses.why: The suffix -ian marks a person attached to something, so the word names one who belongs to the academy.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ian 标记「隶属于某机构的人」，所以这个词指属于学会的人。

senses.title: A scholar or teacher
senses.definition: a scholar, professor, or person connected with formal learning, sometimes with a formal or old-fashioned flavour
senses.definitionCN: 学者、教授或与正规学问相关的人，有时带书卷气
senses.example: The old academician preferred footnotes to headlines.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老学者喜欢脚注胜过头条新闻。
senses.why: Because academy came to mean formal schooling, its person-word extended to anyone living in that world of books.
senses.whyCN: 因为 academy 后来指正规学校，其「人」的称谓便扩展到任何生活在书本世界的人。

intro.en: Academician joins academy with the person suffix -ian, ultimately recalling Plato's grove of Academus.
intro.cn: academician 由 academy 加表示人的后缀 -ian 构成，最终可追溯到柏拉图讲学的阿卡德摩斯园林。

items.en: The grove where Plato taught gave Greek akademia its name.
items.cn: 柏拉图讲学的园林赋予希腊语 akademia 名称。

items.en: Latin adopted the name for the philosophical school.
items.cn: 拉丁语用该名称指这所哲学学校。

items.en: French académie named learned societies from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 académie 自十六世纪起指学术团体。

items.en: Italian formed accademico for a member of such a society.
items.cn: 意大利语造 accademico 指此类团体的成员。

items.en: English borrowed the member-word as academician.
items.cn: 英语借入该「成员」称谓为 academician。

note.en: The first group gathers the academy word family; the second gathers words for learned people.
note.cn: 第一组收 academy 词族；第二组收指学者的词。

entries.definition: Adjective for things related to schools and study.
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，指与学校、学习相关的。

entries.definition: The society or school itself.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指学会或学院本身。

entries.definition: Adverb meaning in terms of study results.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，指在学业成绩方面。

entries.definition: A learned person, often a researcher.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学者」，常指研究者。

entries.definition: A person of deep learning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「博学之士」，书面语。

entries.definition: A senior university teacher.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大学教授」。

entries.definition: A member of a college or learned society.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「（学院或学会的）会员」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the academy root and the -ian suffix; the abstract hooks picture the election ceremony.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 academy 词根与 -ian 后缀；抽象记忆点想象当选仪式。

normal.en: Academy + -ian: the suffix marks a person.
normal.cn: academy 加 -ian：后缀标记人。

normal.en: Compare musician: a person of music, academician: a person of the academy.
normal.cn: 类比 musician（音乐之人），academician 即学会之人。

normal.en: Academies of science elect academicians formally.
normal.cn: 科学院正式选举院士。

normal.en: The stress falls on -mi-: a-ca-de-MI-cian.
normal.cn: 重音落在 -mi- 上。

normal.en: In some countries academician is an honorific title.
normal.cn: 在某些国家，院士是一种荣誉称号。

abstract.en: Picture a certificate with a gold seal naming a new member.
abstract.cn: 想象一张盖着金印的证书，写下新成员之名。

abstract.en: Picture Plato under his trees, surrounded by chosen students.
abstract.cn: 想象柏拉图在园林中，被选中的学生环绕。

abstract.en: Picture an old scholar reading until the lamp burns low.
abstract.cn: 想象老学者读书至灯油耗尽。

examples.en: The academician presented her findings at the annual meeting.
examples.cn: 这位院士在年会上展示了她的研究成果。

examples.en: Only forty academicians sit in that historic society.
examples.cn: 那个历史悠久的学会仅有四十名院士。

examples.en: As a young academician, he wrote with refreshing directness.
examples.cn: 作为年轻学者，他写作直截了当，令人耳目一新。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卡德米先」——进了学会（academy）就是先一步的学者。

root: 希腊语 akademia（柏拉图学园，源自园林名）→ 法语 académie + 意大利语成员后缀 → 英语 academician（学会成员）

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from formal membership in an academy to any scholar living the academic life.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从学会的正式成员，扩展到任何过学术生活的学者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person holding the academy's membership seal
core.cn: 核心意象：手握学会印记的人

branches.en: One formally elected into a learned society.
branches.cn: 被正式选入学术团体的人。

branches.en: One whose daily world is books and research.
branches.cn: 日常世界是书本与研究的人。

branches.en: Both senses sit inside the academy's world of learning.
branches.cn: 两个义项都处于学园的学问世界之内。

branches.en: Membership implies election by one's peers.
branches.cn: 成员身份意味着同行的选举认可。

branches.en: The informal sense sometimes hints at bookish stiffness.
branches.cn: 宽泛义有时暗示书生气。

intro.en: The word adds the person suffix -ian to academy; the family also yields the adjective academic.
intro.cn: 这个词给 academy 加上「人」后缀 -ian；词族还派生形容词 academic。

latinIntro.en: Latin academia preserves the Greek place name, so the Latin entry records the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 academia 保留了希腊地名，拉丁条目记录该名词。

items.meaning: the grove of Academus, learned society
items.meaningCN: 阿卡德摩斯园林；学术团体

形容词，义为「学术的」
副词，义为「在学术上」

definition_zh: 学院；研究院；学会；专门学校
definition_en: a school or society for special training or learning, or an organization that promotes art or science
core_image: 挂满匾额的殿堂：一群人围坐研讨高深学问
scene: 新生穿过大门，墙上刻着创院日期，花园正是两千年前哲人讲学之地。The police academy trains new officers every autumn.
sceneCN: 这里 academy 是「专门学校、训练机构」（第 2 个义项：提供专门训练的学校）；句意为警察学院每年秋天培训新学员。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「学术的；学院的」
由本词加成员后缀构成，义为「院士；学会会员」
同根名词，义为「学术界」

senses.title: A society of scholars or artists
senses.definition: an organization that promotes learning, science, or art and elects distinguished members
senses.definitionCN: 推动学术、科学或艺术并选举杰出成员的组织
senses.example: He read his paper to the Academy of Sciences.
senses.exampleCN: 他向科学院宣读了论文。
senses.why: The oldest use names Plato's school, so the first modern sense keeps the idea of a chosen circle of learned people.
senses.whyCN: 最早的用法指柏拉图的学校，所以第一个现代义项保留了「精选的学者圈子」之意。

senses.title: A school for special training
senses.definition: a school or college for special instruction, such as a military or police academy
senses.definitionCN: 提供专门训练的学校或学院，如军事、警察学院
senses.example: Cadets spend four years at the military academy.
senses.exampleCN: 学员们在军事学院度过四年。
senses.why: The prestige of the old academies made the name attractive to any serious training institution.
senses.whyCN: 古老学园的声望使这个名字受到一切严肃训练机构的青睐。

senses.title: A secondary school
senses.definition: in Britain or America, a private secondary school or a state school of a particular type
senses.definitionCN: 在英国或美国，指私立中学或某类公立学校
senses.example: The academy on the hill takes pupils aged eleven to eighteen.
senses.exampleCN: 山坡上的这所中学招收十一至十八岁的学生。
senses.why: When the word descended to everyday schooling, it kept only the sense of an organized place of teaching.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词下探到日常教育，只保留了「有组织的教学场所」这一层含义。

intro.en: Academy goes back to the grove of Academus near Athens where Plato taught, via Greek akademia and Latin academia.
intro.cn: academy 可追溯到雅典近郊阿卡德摩斯园林——柏拉图讲学之地，经希腊语 akademia 与拉丁语 academia 传入。

items.en: Akademos or Hekademos was the legendary hero of the grove.
items.cn: 阿卡德摩斯是这片园林传说中的英雄，园名源于他。

items.en: akademia named the gymnasium where Plato lectured.
items.cn: akademia 指柏拉图讲学的体育馆兼学园。

items.en: Latin carried the name for the philosophical school.
items.cn: 拉丁语沿用该名称指这所哲学学校。

items.en: Sixteenth-century France used académie for learned societies.
items.cn: 十六世纪的法国用 académie 指学术团体。

items.en: English academy first named Plato's school, then any learned society.
items.cn: 英语 academy 先指柏拉图学园，后泛指学术团体。

items.en: Today the word covers research bodies, training schools, and secondary schools.
items.cn: 今天该词涵盖研究机构、训练学校与中学。

note.en: The first group gathers the same-root family; the second gathers words for places of learning.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词族；第二组收指治学场所的词。

entries.definition: Adjective for study and scholarship.
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，指学术、治学的。

entries.definition: A member of an academy.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指学会成员、院士。

entries.definition: The whole world of colleges and scholars.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指整个学术圈。

entries.definition: An organization for research or teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「研究所；学院」。

entries.definition: A school of higher education.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学院；大学」。

entries.definition: A school for music or arts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「音乐或艺术专门学校」。

entries.definition: An organized group with common interests.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学会；社团」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the grove story and the -y place suffix; the abstract hooks picture the great hall.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用园林典故与表场所的后缀；抽象记忆点想象恢弘大厅。

normal.en: The word is the name of Plato's grove turned into a common noun.
normal.cn: 这个词由柏拉图园林之名变为普通名词。

normal.en: Academy of Sciences elects top scientists as members.
normal.cn: 科学院遴选顶尖科学家为成员。

normal.en: The Oscar is officially an Academy Award.
normal.cn: 奥斯卡奖正式名称为学院奖。

normal.en: The plural changes y to ies: academies.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变 ies：academies。

normal.en: Academy is bigger than a school but need not be a university.
normal.cn: academy 大于一般学校，但不必是大学。

abstract.en: Picture olive trees around students debating under Plato.
abstract.cn: 想象橄榄树下学生围绕柏拉图辩论。

abstract.en: Picture a plaque on a gate carved with a founding date.
abstract.cn: 想象大门上刻着建院日期的铜牌。

abstract.en: Picture a red carpet where the Academy hands out awards.
abstract.cn: 想象学院颁奖时的红毯。

examples.en: She was admitted to the naval academy last year.
examples.cn: 她去年考入了海军学院。

examples.en: The academy publishes its journal twice a year.
examples.cn: 该学会每年出版两期期刊。

examples.en: Local parents petitioned to turn the school into an academy.
examples.cn: 当地家长请愿把这所学校改为学院制学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卡德米」——音译即「学府」，一听就是高深学问之地。

root: 希腊语 Akademos（园林英雄名）→ akademia（柏拉图学园）→ 拉丁语 academia → 法语 académie → 英语 academy（学园；学会；学院）

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a chosen society of scholars, to special training schools, down to ordinary secondary schools.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从精选的学者团体，到专门训练学院，再下探到普通中学。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hall where chosen learners gather
core.cn: 核心意象：被选中者聚学的大厅

branches.en: Elected members advancing science or art.
branches.cn: 推进科学或艺术的选举成员团体。

branches.en: A school dedicated to one profession.
branches.cn: 专攻一种职业的学校。

branches.en: Both keep the ring of formal, serious learning.
branches.cn: 两者都保留正式、严肃治学的意味。

branches.en: The name lent to everyday schooling.
branches.cn: 名字被借给日常学校教育。

branches.en: Every sense is a place or body where teaching is organized.
branches.cn: 每个义项都是组织化教学的场所或机构。

intro.en: The stem is the grove name; suffixes build the adjective, the member word, and the collective noun.
intro.cn: 词干是园林之名；各后缀派生出形容词、成员称谓与集合名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin academia preserves the Greek name directly, so the Latin entry records the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 academia 直接保留希腊名称，拉丁条目记录该名词。

definition_zh: 加速；使加快；促进；提前发生
definition_en: to move or make something move faster, or to make an event happen sooner
core_image: 踏板被踩下，车速表指针向右甩
scene: 司机看到前方路况变好，轻踩油门，车子很快并入快车道。The car accelerated smoothly onto the motorway.
sceneCN: 这里 accelerate 是「加速」（第 1 个义项：使移动速度变快）；句意为车子平稳加速驶入高速公路。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「加速；加速度」
由本词加工具后缀构成，义为「加速器；油门」
由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「加速的；提前的」

senses.title: To move faster
senses.definition: to increase the speed of a vehicle, a process, or a movement
senses.definitionCN: 提高车辆、过程或运动的速度
senses.example: The train accelerated as it left the station.
senses.exampleCN: 火车离站时逐渐加速。
senses.why: Latin accelerare joined ad- 'to' with celer 'swift', so the verb means 'to bring speed to' something.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accelerare 由 ad-（向）与 celer（迅速）组成，因此这个动词意为「把速度加给某物」。

senses.title: To make an event happen sooner
senses.definition: to cause something to occur earlier or more quickly
senses.definitionCN: 使某事更早或更快地发生
senses.example: The new rules accelerated the approval of small projects.
senses.exampleCN: 新规加快了小型项目的审批。
senses.why: The speed image transfers from motion to time: if a process moves faster along its course, its end arrives sooner.
senses.whyCN: 速度意象从运动转到时间：过程在途中走得更快，终点就会更早到达。

senses.title: To gain speed in physics
senses.definition: of a body, to change velocity, especially to increase it
senses.definitionCN: 指物体速度发生变化，尤指增大
senses.example: The particle accelerates as it approaches the field.
senses.exampleCN: 粒子接近场时加速。
senses.why: Physics gives the word a precise measure, acceleration, distinguishing steady motion from changing velocity.
senses.whyCN: 物理学为这个词给出精确的量度 acceleration，把匀速运动与速度变化区分开来。

intro.en: Accelerate is Latin accelerare, from ad- 'to' and celer 'swift, quick'.
intro.cn: accelerate 即拉丁语 accelerare，由 ad-（向）与 celer（迅速）构成。

items.en: celer meant 'swift' and survives in celerity, 'speed'.
items.cn: celer 意为「迅速」，仍见于 celerity（快速）。

items.en: accelerare meant 'to hasten, bring speed to'.
items.cn: accelerare 意为「催促、使加快」。

items.en: acceleratio named the act of hastening.
items.cn: acceleratio 指催促的动作。

items.en: English accelerate first meant to hasten an action or event.
items.cn: 英语 accelerate 最初指催促行动或事件。

items.en: With mechanics, acceleration became a measured change of velocity.
items.cn: 随力学发展，acceleration 成为可测量的速度变化。

items.en: Modern usage extends the verb to economic growth and project schedules.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个动词扩展到经济增长与项目进度。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, the device word, and the participle; the second gathers verbs for increasing speed.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、装置词与分词；第二组收表示提高速度的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for increasing speed, or the rate of change of velocity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加速」或「加速度」。

entries.definition: A device that increases speed, such as a pedal or a machine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加速器、油门」，提高速度的装置。

entries.definition: An adjective for something made faster or moved earlier.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「加速的、提前的」。

entries.definition: A formal noun meaning speed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，正式用法，义为「迅速」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to make something happen sooner.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「促使、加快」。

entries.definition: A phrasal verb meaning to go or make go faster.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「加快」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to make a process run more quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加快办理」，使流程更快。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to become or make quicker.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加快」，变得更迅速。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin 'swift' root and the growth collocations; the abstract hooks picture the needle swinging right.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁语「迅速」词根与增长搭配；抽象记忆点想象指针向右甩。

normal.en: Accelerate holds Latin celer, 'swift', the root of celerity.
normal.cn: accelerate 含有拉丁语 celer（迅速），即 celerity 的词根。

normal.en: Accelerate growth and accelerate the process are the standard patterns.
normal.cn: accelerate growth 与 accelerate the process 是标准搭配。

normal.en: The noun is acceleration, the device an accelerator.
normal.cn: 名词是 acceleration，装置是 accelerator。

normal.en: In physics, acceleration is change of velocity, not just more speed.
normal.cn: 物理学中 acceleration 是速度的变化，不只是变快。

normal.en: The opposite is decelerate, built with de- 'down'.
normal.cn: 反义词是 decelerate，由 de-（向下）构成。

abstract.en: Picture a foot pressing a pedal and the needle leaping right.
abstract.cn: 想象脚踩踏板，指针向右跳。

abstract.en: Picture a queue moving twice as fast after a second window opens.
abstract.cn: 想象第二个窗口开启后队伍快了一倍。

abstract.en: Picture a particle pulled harder as it nears a magnet.
abstract.cn: 想象粒子接近磁体时被拉得更紧。

examples.en: Digital tools have accelerated the pace of research.
examples.cn: 数字工具加快了研究节奏。

examples.en: The bus accelerated away from the stop.
examples.cn: 公交车加速驶离站台。

examples.en: Warmer air accelerates the melting of the glacier.
examples.cn: 较暖的空气加速冰川融化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞勒瑞特」——脚踩油门，指针向右甩，就是加速。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ celer（迅速）→ accelerare（使加快）；核心义是「把速度加上去」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from physical speed, to time saved in a process, to the measured change of velocity in physics.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从物理速度，走到流程中节省的时间，再到物理学中有量度的速度变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle swinging right as the pedal goes down
core.cn: 核心意象：踏板踩下、指针向右甩

branches.en: A vehicle or process moving faster.
branches.cn: 车辆或过程移动得更快。

branches.en: A process reaching its end sooner.
branches.cn: 过程更早到达终点。

branches.en: A physical body whose velocity changes measurably.
branches.cn: 速度发生可测量变化的物体。

branches.en: Speed in motion becomes speed in time.
branches.cn: 运动中的速度转为时间上的提前。

branches.en: Both senses treat speed as something that can be measured and increased.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把速度视为可测量、可提高之物。

intro.en: The verb joins the Latin prefix ad- with the swift root celer-, and its family adds the action, device, and participle endings.
intro.cn: 这个动词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与「迅速」词根 celer- 结合，词族再加动作、装置与分词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin accelerare is the direct ancestor, together with the noun acceleratio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accelerare 是直接祖先，名词 acceleratio 同时。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「加速；加速度」
名词，义为「加速器；油门」

definition_zh: 加速；加速度；增速
definition_en: the process of going faster, or the rate at which speed increases
core_image: 仪表盘上猛抬的速度指针：速度在变大
scene: 绿灯亮起，赛车手踩下油门，指针瞬间冲向表盘右端。The car's acceleration amazed everyone at the track.
sceneCN: 这里 acceleration 是「加速（过程）」（第 1 个义项：速度加快的过程）；句意为这辆车的加速令赛道边所有人惊叹。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「加速」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「加快的」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「加速器；油门」

senses.title: The act of speeding up
senses.definition: the process of starting to move or happen faster
senses.definitionCN: 开始更快移动或更快发生的过程
senses.example: The rocket climbed with smooth acceleration.
senses.exampleCN: 火箭平稳加速攀升。
senses.why: The noun names the action behind the verb accelerate: speed as something that grows, not just is.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名动词 accelerate 背后的动作：速度是被孕育增长的，而非静止不变。

senses.title: The rate of increase in physics
senses.definition: in physics, the change of speed per unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中，单位时间内速度的变化量
senses.example: Earth's gravity gives falling objects an acceleration of about nine point eight metres per second squared.
senses.exampleCN: 地球引力使落体获得约每秒九点八米平方的加速度。
senses.why: Science fixed the loose idea of 'going faster' into an exact quantity: speed divided by time.
senses.whyCN: 科学把「越走越快」的模糊观念精确为确定的量：速度除以时间。

senses.title: An increase in pace of events
senses.definition: a rise in the pace or rate of an activity or development
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动或发展节奏、速率的提升
senses.example: The acceleration of urban change shocked older residents.
senses.exampleCN: 城市变迁的提速让老居民震惊。
senses.why: Anything that can run faster can also develop faster, so the physical image widened to time and history.
senses.whyCN: 任何能跑得更快的东西也可以「发展得更快」，于是物理图像扩展到时间与历史。

intro.en: Acceleration comes from Latin acceleratio, built on accelerare 'to hasten', from ad- 'toward' and celer 'swift'.
intro.cn: acceleration 来自拉丁语 acceleratio，基于 accelerare（使加快），由 ad-（向）与 celer（迅速）构成。

items.en: The root *kel- suggested swift movement, feeding Latin celer.
items.cn: 词根一般认为与「迅速运动」相关，成为拉丁语 celer 的来源。

items.en: celer meant swift, as in celeritas 'speed'.
items.cn: celer 意为迅速，如 celeritas（速度）。

items.en: ad- plus celerare meant to hasten something.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 加 celerare 意为使某物加快。

items.en: The noun acceleratio named the hastening itself.
items.cn: 名词 acceleratio 指加快这一行为本身。

items.en: English took the word, and physics later gave it exact meaning.
items.cn: 英语借入该词，物理学后来赋予其精确含义。

note.en: The first group gathers the celer- word family; the second gathers words for speeding up.
note.cn: 第一组收 celer- 词族；第二组收表示提速的词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同根动词，即本词的基础。

entries.definition: A device or pedal that speeds things up.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指加速器或油门。

entries.definition: Swiftness of movement, from the same Latin stem.
entries.definitionCN: 同根书面语名词，义为「迅速」。

entries.definition: An increase in speed, often informal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「提速」，多口语。

entries.definition: Quickness of action, with a hint of rushing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「匆忙」，带仓促意味。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to become faster.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加快」。

entries.definition: The rate of slowing down.
entries.definitionCN: 反义名词，义为「减速」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the swift root celer and the physics formula; the abstract hooks picture the needle climbing.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「迅速」词根 celer 与物理公式；抽象记忆点想象指针攀升。

normal.en: Break it as ac-celer-ation: celer means swift in Latin.
normal.cn: 拆为 ac-celer-ation：celer 在拉丁语中意为迅速。

normal.en: The -ion ending turns the verb accelerate into a noun.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ion 把动词 accelerate 变为名词。

normal.en: In physics, acceleration equals change of speed over time.
normal.cn: 物理学中，加速度等于速度变化除以时间。

normal.en: Gravity's acceleration on Earth is about nine point eight.
normal.cn: 地球重力加速度约为九点八。

normal.en: Pressing the accelerator pedal gives the car acceleration.
normal.cn: 踩下油门（accelerator）使车获得加速度。

abstract.en: Picture a speedometer needle sweeping to the right.
abstract.cn: 想象速度表指针向右猛扫。

abstract.en: Picture a falling apple gaining speed each second.
abstract.cn: 想象落下的苹果每秒都在提速。

abstract.en: Picture a city changing faster every year.
abstract.cn: 想象城市逐年加速变迁。

examples.en: The train's acceleration pinned passengers gently to their seats.
examples.cn: 列车的加速让乘客轻微地压向椅背。

examples.en: Engineers measured the acceleration of the prototype on the test track.
examples.cn: 工程师在试验道上测量了样车的加速度。

examples.en: Economists debated whether the acceleration of growth could last.
examples.cn: 经济学家争论增长的提速能否持续。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞勒雷申」——谐音「可加速了的申（请）」，一踩油门就提速。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ celer（迅速）→ accelerare（使加快）→ acceleratio（加速）；核心义是「速度向快处推进」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the everyday act of speeding up, to the exact physics quantity, to the pace of change in life.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从日常的提速行为，到精确的物理学量，再到生活变迁的节奏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: speed that is not fixed but growing
core.cn: 核心意象：速度不固定，而是在增长

branches.en: A vehicle or process starting to run faster.
branches.cn: 车辆或过程开始跑得更快。

branches.en: Speed change fixed as a measurable quantity.
branches.cn: 速度变化被固化为可测的量。

branches.en: Both senses describe speed as something that increases.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把速度描述为在增加的东西。

branches.en: The faster rhythm of cities, markets, and history.
branches.cn: 城市、市场与历史更快的节奏。

branches.en: Exact measure in physics, loose measure in social change.
branches.cn: 物理中的精确度量，社会变迁中的宽泛度量。

intro.en: The word joins the toward-prefix with the swift stem and the action noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由「向」前缀、「迅速」词干与动作名词后缀组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin celer and acceleratio are direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the stem and the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 celer 与 acceleratio 是直接祖先，拉丁条目记录词干与名词。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「加速」
名词，义为「加速器；油门」
形容词，义为「加快的」

definition_zh: 通道；入口；使用权；接触机会；进入；接入；访问；存取
definition_en: a way of entering a place, the right to use or reach something, or the act of reaching or opening it
core_image: 一扇只配了一把钥匙的侧门：能不能进去，全看钥匙在不在你手里
scene: 老小区的正门封了，住户每天都要绕到后街。The only access to the garden is through a narrow gate.
sceneCN: 这里 access 指「进入的通道」（第 1 个义项：可以进入某处的路径或门）；句意为通往花园的唯一通道是一扇窄门。

pos.zh: 名词：通道；使用权；接触机会；接入
动词：进入；接近；访问；存取

collocations.zh: 通往……的通道；使用……的机会

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -ible 构成，义为「可到达的；可使用的；易懂的」
由 accessible 加后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可达性；无障碍程度」
由否定前缀 in- 加 accessible 构成，义为「难以到达的；难以理解的」
由同一拉丁词根加后缀 -ion 构成，义为「就职；加入；新增」

senses.title: A way in or through
senses.definition: a path, door, road, or other route by which a place can be entered or reached
senses.definitionCN: 指进入或抵达某处的路径、门、道路等
senses.example: The only access to the village is by boat.
senses.exampleCN: 进入这个村子唯一的通道是坐船。
senses.why: Latin accessus was a coming near; a way in is the route that lets that approach happen.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessus 意为「走近」；通道就是让这种走近得以发生的路线。

senses.title: The right to use or obtain
senses.definition: the right or opportunity to use, see, or obtain something that is limited or controlled
senses.definitionCN: 指使用、查看或取得受限事物的权利或机会
senses.example: Every student has access to the online library.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学生都能使用在线图书馆。
senses.why: If a route is open to you, you may walk along it; the route quietly turns into a permission.
senses.whyCN: 如果一条路对你敞开，你就可以沿着它走过去；路线于是悄悄变成了许可。

senses.title: The act of getting in
senses.definition: the act of entering a place or of reaching a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 指进入某地或接触到某人、某物的行为
senses.example: Reporters were refused access to the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 记者被拒绝进入会场。
senses.why: The noun shifts from the route to the movement along it: the approach itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词从「路线」转到「沿路线移动」：也就是走近这个动作本身。

senses.title: A connection to a system
senses.definition: the ability of a device or user to connect to the internet, a network, or a service
senses.definitionCN: 指设备或用户连接互联网、网络或服务的能力
senses.example: The hotel offers free internet access in every room.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆每个房间都提供免费网络接入。
senses.why: A network is treated like a building: you need a way in before you can use what is inside.
senses.whyCN: 网络被当作一栋建筑：先有进去的路，才能使用里面的东西。

senses.title: To reach or enter
senses.definition: to reach, enter, or make use of a place, especially one that is restricted
senses.definitionCN: 指进入、抵达或使用某地，尤指受限之处
senses.example: Staff can access the lab with their ID cards.
senses.exampleCN: 工作人员可以用工牌进入实验室。
senses.why: The verb turns the route into motion: walking the way in.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「路线」变成动作：沿着进去的路走。

senses.title: To open stored data
senses.definition: to open, read, or retrieve files or data stored in a computer system
senses.definitionCN: 指打开、读取或调取计算机系统中存储的文件或数据
senses.example: You can access your files from any device.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以从任何设备访问自己的文件。
senses.why: Data is stored behind a system, and reaching it follows the same pattern as reaching a room.
senses.whyCN: 数据存放在系统之后，取到它的方式和走进一个房间是同一种模式。

senses.title: A sudden fit of feeling
senses.definition: a sudden outburst of an emotion, an old and mostly literary use
senses.definitionCN: 指情绪的突然爆发，属古老且多用于文学的用法
senses.example: In an access of rage, he tore the letter in two.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵暴怒之下，他把信撕成两半。
senses.why: Latin accessus also meant an onset, as if a feeling came upon a person and entered him.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessus 也有「来袭、发作」之意，仿佛一种情绪扑上来，进入了人。

senses.title: Used before a noun for a route
senses.definition: placed before another noun to name a road, code, or point that gives entry
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词之前，表示提供进入的道路、密码或地点
senses.example: Turn left at the access road behind the station.
senses.exampleCN: 在车站后面的辅路向左转。
senses.why: The route sense is compressed into a modifier: a road whose whole job is to give access.
senses.whyCN: 「路线」这一义被压缩成修饰语：一条存在意义就是提供通行的路。

intro.en: Access comes from a Latin verb of going, and the noun still keeps the shape of a doorway.
intro.cn: access 来自一个表示「走」的拉丁语动词，名词至今仍保留「门口」的形状。

items.en: The verb cedere meant 'to go, move, yield'. Its earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 cedere 意为「走、移动、让出」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus cedere formed accedere, 'to come near, approach; to be added'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 cedere 构成 accedere，意为「走近、接近；附加」。

items.en: The noun accessus meant 'a coming near, an entrance', and also 'an increase'.
items.cn: 名词 accessus 意为「接近、入口」，同时也有「增加」之义。

items.en: Old French acces brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century with the senses of approach and entrance.
items.cn: 古法语 acces 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，带有「接近」与「入口」两义。

items.en: The verb is much later and is generally dated to the twentieth century; the computing sense grew with the computer.
items.cn: 动词用法晚得多，一般追溯到二十世纪；计算机「存取数据」义随电脑普及而发展。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root of going and reaching; the near-meaning group names ways of entering or being admitted.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「走、抵达」的拉丁词根；近义组列出「进入」与「获准进入」的各种说法。

entries.definition: Able to be reached, entered, or used, also used of places designed for disabled people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可到达的、可使用的」，也指为残障人士设计的无障碍场所。

entries.definition: The noun for how easy something is to reach or use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可达性、无障碍程度」，指某处或某物被到达和使用的容易程度。

entries.definition: Too far, too difficult, or too locked to be reached.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以到达的、难以理解的」，是 accessible 加否定前缀构成的反义形式。

entries.definition: The act of taking up an office or of joining a group, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就职、加入、新增」，来自同一个拉丁语动词。

entries.definition: The door or opening by which you enter, more physical than access.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「入口、门口」，比 access 更强调具体的门或开口。

entries.definition: The act of going in, or the right to go in, often in official contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入、入场权」，常用于较正式的语境。

entries.definition: Permission to enter a place or join an institution, often after a check.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「准许进入、录取」，通常需要经过查验或审核。

entries.definition: The act of coming near, or a way of dealing with something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「接近、途径」，也可指处理问题的方法。

entries.definition: To arrive at or stretch out to something, with no idea of permission.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「到达、伸手够到」，不含「获准」的意思。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb of going and the everyday phrases built on access.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「走」动词，以及由 access 构成的日常搭配。

normal.en: cedere is to go: access is the going up to a place.
normal.cn: cedere 是「走」：access 就是朝某处走过去。

normal.en: Accedere adds ad- 'to', so the word always points at a destination.
normal.cn: accedere 加了 ad-「向」，所以这个词总是指向一个目的地。

normal.en: Access to a place is a route; access to a thing is a right.
normal.cn: access to a place 是路线，access to a thing 则是权利。

normal.en: An access code is the modern key to the old door.
normal.cn: access code 就是开那扇老门的新式钥匙。

normal.en: The verb keeps the same shape: access a file, access a building.
normal.cn: 动词形式完全一样：access a file 是访问文件，access a building 是进入大楼。

abstract.en: A door, a key, and a hand on the handle: permission is only a route that stayed open.
abstract.cn: 一扇门、一把钥匙、一只搭在门把上的手：许可不过是一条没有关上的路。

abstract.en: The same word covers a garden gate and a folder on a screen, because both stand between you and what you want.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指花园小门，也指屏幕上的文件夹，因为两者都挡在你和想要的东西之间。

abstract.en: Access is never the thing itself; it is the thin passage that leads to it.
abstract.cn: access 从来不是东西本身，它只是通向那件东西的细窄通道。

examples.en: Students have free access to the online library.
examples.cn: 学生可以免费使用在线图书馆。

examples.en: You can access your files from any device.
examples.cn: 你可以从任何设备访问自己的文件。

examples.en: The rear door gives access to the garden.
examples.cn: 后门通向花园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾克塞斯」——走到门口，门恰好开了：能走进去就是 access。

root: 拉丁语 accessus「接近、入口」来自 accedere「走近」，由 ad-「向」加 cedere「走、让」构成；更早的词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Access starts as a physical way in and spreads to permission, to networks, to stored data, and even to a feeling that suddenly comes over a person.
sensesIntro.cn: access 从一条实在的进门之路出发，扩展到许可、网络、存储的数据，甚至扩展到突然扑上心头的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a locked side door; a key turns and the way in appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇锁着的侧门，钥匙一转，进去的路出现了。

branches.en: THE DOOR: a route into a place, and the act of walking through it.
branches.cn: 门口线：进入某处的路线，以及穿过去的动作。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: an open route becomes a permission, and the permission becomes an act.
branches.cn: 权利线：敞开的路线变成许可，许可又变成一次具体的进入。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: a network and its stored files are reached the way a room is reached.
branches.cn: 系统线：网络与其中存储的文件，都按走进房间的方式来抵达。

branches.en: THE ONSET: an emotion arrives and enters a person, an old literary branch.
branches.cn: 发作线：情绪来临并进入一个人，这是古老的文学分支。

branches.en: THE MODIFIER: the route sense shrinks into a word placed before a noun.
branches.cn: 定语线：路线义缩小成一个放在名词前的修饰词。

intro.cn: access 是一个表示运动的拉丁语名词，英语靠后缀而不是新词根扩展它的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb cedere, its compound accedere and the noun accessus are all recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 cedere、它的复合形式 accedere 与名词 accessus 均有文献记录。

items.meaning: a coming near, a way in
items.exampleCN: 只有工作人员可以进入。

items.example: The variant appears in process and access.
items.exampleCN: 这个变体出现在 process 与 access 中。

可达性；无障碍程度
