definition_zh: 可到达的；易得到的；易理解的；无障碍的
definition_en: easy to reach, easy to obtain or use, easy to understand, or designed for people with disabilities
core_image: 一条坡道让轮椅也能顺利进门
scene: 博物馆把正门旁加了缓坡，轮椅和婴儿车都能直接推进展厅。The new entrance makes the gallery accessible to everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 accessible 是「可进入的、无障碍的」（第 1 个义项：容易到达）；句意为新入口让所有人都能进入展厅。

pos.zh: 可到达的；易得到的；易理解的；无障碍的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「可及性；无障碍程度」
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「易懂地」
同源名词，义为「通道；使用权」

senses.title: Easy to reach
senses.definition: of a place, able to be reached without difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 指某地不难到达
senses.example: The beach is accessible only by boat.
senses.exampleCN: 这片海滩只能乘船到达。
senses.why: The adjective adds -ible, 'can be', to access, so it describes a place where the way in actually works.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在 access 上加 -ible（能够被），因此描述入口真正行得通的地方。

senses.title: Easy to obtain or use
senses.definition: of a service, resource, or price, within most people's reach
senses.definitionCN: 指服务、资源或价格在多数人可及范围内
senses.example: Affordable housing should be accessible to young families.
senses.exampleCN: 可负担住房应当让年轻家庭够得着。
senses.why: Physical reach extends to cost and permission: if nothing blocks the way, the thing is accessible even without a door.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的可及扩展到费用与许可：若没有阻碍，即使没有门，该物也是可获取的。

senses.title: Easy to understand
senses.definition: of writing or speech, clear enough for non-specialists
senses.definitionCN: 指文字或言语清楚到非专业者也能懂
senses.example: She writes in accessible language without losing accuracy.
senses.exampleCN: 她用通俗的语言写作，又不失准确。
senses.why: Understanding is pictured as entering a text; when the door is wide, the reader walks in without a key.
senses.whyCN: 理解被想象为走进文本；门开得宽，读者不用钥匙就能进去。

senses.title: Designed for disabled users
senses.definition: built or fitted so that people with disabilities can use it
senses.definitionCN: 为残障人士使用而建造或改装
senses.example: The station has lifts and an accessible toilet.
senses.exampleCN: 车站设有电梯和无障碍卫生间。
senses.why: Modern design gives the old word a technical sense: a building is accessible when no physical barrier shuts a group out.
senses.whyCN: 现代设计给这个词一个技术义：当没有物理障碍把某群体挡在外面，建筑就是无障碍的。

intro.en: Accessible is access with the Latin possibility suffix -ibilis, meaning 'that can be entered'.
intro.cn: accessible 是 access 加拉丁语可能性后缀 -ibilis，意为「能够被进入的」。

items.en: cedere meant 'to go', the root of accedere and accessus.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走」，是 accedere 与 accessus 的词根。

items.en: accessus meant 'a coming near, an approach'.
items.cn: accessus 意为「走近、接近」。

items.en: The suffix -ibilis marked what is possible or fit to be done.
items.cn: 后缀 -ibilis 标记可能或适合被做之事。

items.en: French formed accessible with the sense 'that can be approached'.
items.cn: 法语构成 accessible，义为「可以被接近的」。

items.en: English accessible first described places that could be entered.
items.cn: 英语 accessible 先描述可以进入的场所。

items.en: Modern usage adds easy reading and barrier-free design.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了易读与无障碍设计两层意思。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adverb, and base noun; the second gathers adjectives for what is within reach.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、副词与基础名词；第二组收表示可及范围的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for how easily something can be reached or used.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可及性」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in an easy-to-reach or easy-to-read way'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「易懂地、可及地」。

entries.definition: The noun for a way in or a right to use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通道；使用权」。

entries.definition: The negative adjective for what cannot be reached.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词否定形式，义为「无法到达的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for a place one can get to.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可到达的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for something ready to be used or obtained.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可获得的、可用的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for something clear enough to grasp.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可理解的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for something not closed to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「开放的」，对公众不封闭。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -ible 'can be' rule and the wheelchair phrases; the abstract hooks picture a ramp beside a steep step.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 -ible「能够被」规则与无障碍搭配；抽象记忆点想象陡台阶旁的缓坡。

normal.en: Accessible is access plus -ible: able to be entered.
normal.cn: accessible 是 access 加 -ible：能够被进入。

normal.en: Accessible to is the fixed preposition: accessible to all.
normal.cn: accessible to 是固定介词结构：accessible to all。

normal.en: Wheelchair accessible is a standard design label.
normal.cn: wheelchair accessible 是标准设计标签。

normal.en: The noun is accessibility, the adverb accessibly.
normal.cn: 名词是 accessibility，副词是 accessibly。

normal.en: The negative is inaccessible, with in- prefixed.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 inaccessible，加前缀 in-。

abstract.en: Picture a gentle ramp beside a steep stone step.
abstract.cn: 想象陡石阶旁的一条缓坡。

abstract.en: Picture a journal with no paywall in front of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本前面没有付费墙的期刊。

abstract.en: Picture a guidebook that explains jargon in plain words.
abstract.cn: 想象一本用大白话解释术语的指南。

examples.en: The temple is accessible by a footpath from the village.
examples.cn: 从村子沿小路可以到达这座庙。

examples.en: The library makes rare books accessible online.
examples.cn: 图书馆让珍本可以在线获取。

examples.en: Her lecture was accessible to students without a science background.
examples.cn: 她的讲座让没有理科背景的学生也听得懂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞斯波」——门口加了缓坡，谁都能进去，就是可到达的。

root: 拉丁语 accedere（走近）+ -ibilis（能够被）；核心义是「进得去、够得着、读得懂」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a place one can reach, to a resource one can use, to a text one can understand, to a building open to disabled users.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从能到达的场所，走到能使用的资源，再到能读懂的文本，最后是对残障者开放的建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ramp that removes the barrier at the door
core.cn: 核心意象：消除门口障碍的缓坡

branches.en: A place whose way in actually works.
branches.cn: 入口真正行得通的场所。

branches.en: A service or price within most people's reach.
branches.cn: 多数人够得着的服务或价格。

branches.en: Writing clear enough for a non-specialist.
branches.cn: 非专业者也能读懂的写作。

branches.en: A building with no physical barrier for disabled users.
branches.cn: 对残障使用者没有物理障碍的建筑。

branches.en: The general sense and the design sense both remove obstacles.
branches.cn: 一般义与设计义都在消除障碍。

intro.en: The word joins the going root ced- with the prefix ad- and the possibility suffix -ible, and its family adds noun and adverb forms.
intro.cn: 这个词把「走」词根 ced- 与前缀 ad-、可能性后缀 -ible 结合，词族另加名词与副词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin accedere plus -ibilis produced the form, so the Latin entries record the verb and the suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accedere 加 -ibilis 构成此形，因此拉丁条目记录动词与后缀。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「可及性；无障碍程度」
副词，义为「易懂地」

definition_zh: 配件；饰品；附件；从犯；附加的
definition_en: an extra item that completes something, or a person who helps another commit a crime
core_image: 一套衣服之外再添的一条围巾、一只包
scene: 她穿素色长裙，只加了一枚旧胸针，整个造型立刻完整。A simple brooch was her only accessory.
sceneCN: 这里 accessory 是「饰品、配件」（第 1 个义项：起补充作用的附加物件）；句意为一枚简单的胸针是她唯一的配饰。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀构成，义为「搭配饰物」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「配以饰物的」

senses.title: An extra item that completes a look
senses.definition: an item such as a bag, belt, or jewellery worn to complete an outfit
senses.definitionCN: 包、腰带或首饰之类，用来完善整体装束的物件
senses.example: She keeps her accessories simple: one ring and a plain scarf.
senses.exampleCN: 她的配饰很简单：一枚戒指和一条素色围巾。
senses.why: Latin accessorius meant 'that which comes alongside'; an accessory stands beside the main thing and completes it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessorius 意为「随之而来的」；配件站在主物旁边，把它补充完整。

senses.title: An additional part for a device
senses.definition: an optional part that adds function to a machine or tool
senses.definitionCN: 为机器或工具增加功能的可选部件
senses.example: The shop sells lenses and other camera accessories.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售镜头与其他相机配件。
senses.why: The same 'coming alongside' logic applies to machines: the part does not work alone but extends what the main device can do.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「在旁边」逻辑适用于机器：配件不能单独工作，只是扩展主设备的功能。

senses.title: A person who helps in a crime
senses.definition: a person who assists another in committing an offence without being the principal
senses.definitionCN: 协助他人实施犯罪、但非主犯的人
senses.example: He was charged as an accessory to the robbery.
senses.exampleCN: 他被指控为抢劫案的从犯。
senses.why: Legal Latin used accessorius for a person standing beside the main actor, so the criminal sense keeps the idea of help from the side.
senses.whyCN: 法律拉丁语用 accessorius 指站在主行为人旁边的人，因此罪案义保留了「从旁协助」的意思。

senses.title: Additional and subordinate
senses.definition: existing to support something more important
senses.definitionCN: 为支持更重要之物而存在
senses.example: The firm treats training as an accessory service, not a core one.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司把培训当作附加服务，而非核心业务。
senses.why: The adjective generalizes the noun: anything that only supports a main thing can be called accessory.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把名词一般化：任何只起支持主物作用的东西都可称为附加的。

intro.en: Accessory comes from Latin accessorius, 'that which comes alongside', from accedere, 'to go toward'.
intro.cn: accessory 来自拉丁语 accessorius（随之而来的），源自动词 accedere（走向）。

items.en: cedere meant 'to go', the root behind access and accede.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走」，是 access 与 accede 的词根。

items.en: accedere meant 'to go toward, come alongside'.
items.cn: accedere 意为「走向、从旁而来」。

items.en: accessor named a person who comes alongside, often as a helper.
items.cn: accessor 指从旁而来的人，常为帮手。

items.en: accessorius meant 'belonging to one who comes alongside'.
items.cn: accessorius 意为「属于从旁而来者的」。

items.en: English accessory first appeared in legal language for a helper in a case.
items.cn: 英语 accessory 先出现在法律语言中，指案中帮手。

items.en: Modern usage adds clothing items and optional device parts.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了服饰单品与可选设备部件。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb and participle from the same family; the second gathers words for added items and helpers.
note.cn: 第一组收同族动词与分词；第二组收表示附加物与帮手的词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to add accessories to an outfit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「给装束搭配饰物」。

entries.definition: An adjective for an outfit completed with accessories.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「配以饰物的」。

entries.definition: The noun and verb for a way in or the act of reaching.
entries.definitionCN: 名词与动词，义为「通道」或「访问」。

entries.definition: An extra part fixed to a device.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附加装置」，固定在设备上的部件。

entries.definition: Something added to improve or complete.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附加物」，为改进或完善而添加。

entries.definition: A person who helps another commit a crime.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「共犯」，协助他人犯罪的人。

entries.definition: An item added for beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「装饰品」，为美观而添加。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'comes alongside' origin and the fashion phrases; the abstract hooks picture a plain dress completed by one brooch.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「从旁而来」来源与服饰搭配；抽象记忆点想象一枚胸针补全素色长裙。

normal.en: Accessory is Latin 'comes alongside' the main thing.
normal.cn: accessory 是拉丁语「从旁而来」，伴随主物。

normal.en: Fashion accessories and car accessories are the two shopping phrases.
normal.cn: fashion accessories 与 car accessories 是两个购物短语。

normal.en: An accessory to a crime is a helper, not the main actor.
normal.cn: an accessory to a crime 是帮凶，不是主犯。

normal.en: The plural is accessories, and the verb is accessorize.
normal.cn: 复数是 accessories，动词是 accessorize。

normal.en: Accessory as an adjective means subordinate or supporting.
normal.cn: accessory 作形容词意为附属的、辅助的。

abstract.en: Picture a plain dress completed by one old brooch.
abstract.cn: 想象素色长裙因一枚旧胸针而完整。

abstract.en: Picture a camera with an extra lens clipped on.
abstract.cn: 想象相机上多挂了一支镜头。

abstract.en: Picture a driver waiting outside while another enters the bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在外开车等候，另一人进银行。

examples.en: The belt is sold as an accessory, not part of the suit.
examples.cn: 这条腰带作为配件出售，不含在套装内。

examples.en: Phone accessories fill two shelves in the shop.
examples.cn: 手机配件占了店里两个货架。

examples.en: He was convicted as an accessory to the fraud.
examples.cn: 他作为诈骗案的从犯被定罪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞瑟瑞」——站在主物旁边、给它补上最后一笔的小物件，就是配件。

root: 拉丁语 accedere（从旁而来）+ -orius（属于……的）；核心义是「从旁补充主物之物」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a worn item that completes an outfit, to an optional device part, to a person who helps in a crime, to the general adjective 'supporting'.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从完善装束的佩戴物，走到可选的设备部件，再到罪案中的帮手，最后是形容词「附属的」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small item standing beside the main thing
core.cn: 核心意象：站在主物旁边的一件小物

branches.en: A worn item that finishes an outfit.
branches.cn: 完成整套装束的佩戴物。

branches.en: An optional part that extends a device.
branches.cn: 扩展设备功能的可选部件。

branches.en: A person who assists the main actor in a crime.
branches.cn: 在犯罪中协助主行为人者。

branches.en: Anything that only supports something more important.
branches.cn: 任何只支持更重要之物的东西。

branches.en: Fashion and hardware both add a piece beside the main item.
branches.cn: 服饰与硬件都在主物旁添加一件东西。

intro.en: The word joins the going root ced- with the prefix ad- and the relational ending -ory, and its family adds a verb and participle.
intro.cn: 这个词把「走」词根 ced- 与前缀 ad-、关系后缀 -ory 结合，词族另加动词与分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin accessorius is the direct ancestor, formed from accessor, so the Latin entries record the noun and the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accessorius 是直接祖先，由 accessor 构成，因此拉丁条目记录名词与形容词。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「搭配饰物」
形容词，义为「配以饰物的」

definition_zh: 使适应（新环境）；服水土
definition_en: to become used to a new place, climate, or situation
core_image: 候鸟落在新枝头：一点点调整自己融入新环境
scene: 高原的新兵头几天喘不上气，两周后已能轻松跑完全程。It took him weeks to acclimate to the high altitude.
sceneCN: 这里 acclimate 是「适应新环境」（第 1 个义项：让身体习惯新条件）；句意为他花了几周才适应高原环境。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「适应；服水土」
同源变体，义为「使适应气候」

senses.title: To adjust to a climate or place
senses.definition: to let body or mind become used to new surroundings or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 让身体或心理习惯新的环境或条件
senses.example: The plants acclimated quickly to the greenhouse.
senses.exampleCN: 这些植物很快适应了温室环境。
senses.why: The word was first used of plants and climate; the core idea is a living thing settling into new conditions.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初用于植物与气候；核心观念是生命体在新条件中安顿下来。

senses.title: To adjust to a new situation
senses.definition: to become comfortable in a new job, culture, or way of life
senses.definitionCN: 在新工作、文化或生活方式中变得自在
senses.example: New hires usually acclimate within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工通常一个月内就能适应。
senses.why: If a body can settle into new weather, a mind can settle into new circumstances, so the word stretched to life changes.
senses.whyCN: 身体能安顿于新天气，心理也能安顿于新境遇，于是这个词扩展到生活变化。

intro.en: Acclimate is a French-style blend of acclimatize, joining ad- 'toward' with climat 'climate'.
intro.cn: acclimate 是 acclimatize 的法语式简化，由 ad-（向）与 climat（气候）拼合。

items.en: klima meant the slope of the ground, later its weather zone.
items.cn: 希腊语 klima 指地面的坡度，后指其气候带。

items.en: French climat narrowed to mean weather conditions.
items.cn: 法语 climat 收窄为指天气状况。

items.en: acclimater meant to habituate to a climate.
items.cn: 法语 acclimater 意为使习惯于某气候。

items.en: English formed acclimatize in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪造出 acclimatize。

items.en: The shorter acclimate is now standard American usage.
items.cn: 较短的 acclimate 是如今美式标准用法。

note.en: The first group gathers the climate word family; the second gathers verbs for adapting.
note.cn: 第一组收气候词族；第二组收表示适应的动词。

entries.definition: The longer British-style variant of the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的较长英式变体。

entries.definition: The noun for the process of adapting.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，指适应的过程。

entries.definition: The usual weather of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指一地的气候。

entries.definition: To change oneself to fit new conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「适应；改造自己以配合新条件」。

entries.definition: To make small changes to fit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调整以适应」。

entries.definition: To make used to something by repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 书面语动词，义为「使习惯于」。

entries.definition: To become comfortable in a new home or place.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「安顿下来」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the climate root and the a- prefix; the abstract hooks picture gradual settling.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 climate 词根与前缀 a-；抽象记忆点想象逐步安顿的过程。

normal.en: See climate inside the word: the core meaning is adjusting to climate.
normal.cn: 词中有 climate：核心义就是适应气候。

normal.en: A- is a reduced form of ad-, meaning toward.
normal.cn: a- 是 ad- 的弱化形式，意为「向」。

normal.en: Acclimatize is the longer British twin of acclimate.
normal.cn: acclimatize 是 acclimate 较长的英式孪生词。

normal.en: The noun acclimation names the settling process.
normal.cn: 名词 acclimation 指安顿适应的过程。

normal.en: Both people and plants can acclimate.
normal.cn: 人和植物都可以 acclimate。

abstract.en: Picture a transplanted tree slowly growing new roots.
abstract.cn: 想象移栽的树慢慢长出新根。

abstract.en: Picture a climber pausing each day to let the mountain feel normal.
abstract.cn: 想象登山者每天停一停，让高海拔慢慢变得平常。

abstract.en: Picture a new student finding their seat in an unfamiliar hall.
abstract.cn: 想象新生在陌生礼堂里找到自己的位置。

examples.en: A month in the city was enough to acclimate her to the noise.
examples.cn: 在城里待上一个月就足以让她适应噪音。

examples.en: Farmers acclimate seedlings before planting them outdoors.
examples.cn: 农民在把幼苗移到户外前先让它们适应环境。

examples.en: It is easier to acclimate when you keep a routine.
examples.cn: 保持作息规律更容易适应新环境。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克克里买特」——到了新地方先「买」点当地的「特」产，慢慢就习惯了。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ 希腊语 klima 经法语 climat（气候）→ acclimater（使习惯于气候）→ 英语 acclimate（使适应）

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from adjusting to a physical climate, to adjusting to any new situation.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从适应自然气候，扩展到适应任何新处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a living thing slowly rooting into new conditions
core.cn: 核心意象：生命体慢慢在新条件中扎根

branches.en: Body or plant settling into new air and weather.
branches.cn: 身体或植物在新空气与天气中安顿。

branches.en: Mind settling into new work or culture.
branches.cn: 心理在新工作或文化中安顿。

branches.en: Both senses are the same settling at different depths.
branches.cn: 两个义项是同一种安顿在不同层面的体现。

branches.en: Adjustment takes time and gentle repetition.
branches.cn: 适应需要时间与温和的重复。

branches.en: Comfort grows as the unfamiliar turns routine.
branches.cn: 当陌生变成日常，自在随之生长。

intro.en: The word joins the toward-prefix with the climate stem and a verb ending; the family adds a noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由「向」前缀、「气候」词干与动词结尾组成；词族另派生名词。

latinIntro.en: The climate stem travelled through Latin and French, so the Latin entry records the borrowed noun.
latinIntro.cn: 「气候」词干经拉丁语与法语传播，拉丁条目记录借入的名词。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「适应；服水土」
动词，义为「使适应气候」

definition_zh: 荣誉；嘉奖；赞扬
definition_en: an award, honour, or strong praise given to someone
core_image: 金杯举过头顶：掌声落在受奖者肩头
scene: 颁奖台上灯光亮起，全场起立，她的名字被念出三次。The young director received the highest accolade of the festival.
sceneCN: 这里 accolade 是「荣誉、嘉奖」（第 1 个义项：公开授予的奖励或赞誉）；句意为这位年轻导演获得电影节最高荣誉。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加过去分词后缀构成的罕见形容词，义为「受到嘉奖的」
由本词加复数后缀构成，新闻语体常用，义为「接连的荣誉」

senses.title: An award or public praise
senses.definition: an honour, prize, or enthusiastic public approval given for achievement
senses.definitionCN: 因成就而获得的荣誉、奖励或热烈的公开赞许
senses.example: The novel earned accolades from every reviewer.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说赢得了所有评论者的赞誉。
senses.why: The old ceremony of touching the shoulder became the image of any formal act of honour.
senses.whyCN: 古人触肩授爵的仪式，成为一切正式授荣行为的意象来源。

senses.title: The knighting ceremony
senses.definition: in history, the ceremonial embrace or shoulder touch used when making a knight
senses.definitionCN: 历史上册封骑士时拥抱或触肩的仪式
senses.example: The king performed the accolade with a light tap of the sword.
senses.exampleCN: 国王以剑轻触肩膀行册封礼。
senses.why: This is the original sense: the physical gesture on the neck or shoulders that marked a new knight.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：在颈肩上做出标志新骑士的实体动作。

intro.en: Accolade comes through French from Latin accolade, 'an embrace around the neck', from ad- 'to' and collum 'neck'.
intro.cn: accolade 经法语来自拉丁语 accolade（环颈拥抱），由 ad-（向）与 collum（颈）构成。

items.en: collum meant neck, as in collar.
items.cn: collum 意为颈，如 collar（衣领）。

items.en: accolade meant an embrace about the neck.
items.cn: 拉丁语 accolade 意为环颈拥抱。

items.en: The word named the embrace in the knighting rite.
items.cn: 法语 accolade 指册封骑士礼中的拥抱。

items.en: English borrowed it first for the ceremony itself.
items.cn: 英语借入时首先指册封仪式。

items.en: The sense widened to any honour or loud praise.
items.cn: 词义扩大为任何荣誉或盛赞。

note.en: The first group gathers the neck-root family; the second gathers words for honours.
note.cn: 第一组收「颈」词根词族；第二组收表示荣誉的词。

entries.definition: A band for the neck, from the same Latin stem.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指衣领、项圈。

entries.definition: A neckline of a dress, from the French use of the neck word.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指女装的露颈领口。

entries.definition: An official paper; only spelling-similar, different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指证书；仅拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Great respect or an award for merit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荣誉；敬意」。

entries.definition: A prize given for achievement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「奖项」。

entries.definition: An act or statement honouring someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「颂词；致敬」。

entries.definition: Honours won, pictured as a wreath.
entries.definitionCN: 文学化名词，义为「桂冠；荣誉」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the neck root and the knighting scene; the abstract hooks picture the stage and the applause.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「颈」词根与册封场景；抽象记忆点想象颁奖台与掌声。

normal.en: The root collum means neck: the old accolade embraced the neck.
normal.cn: 词根 collum 意为颈：古老的册封礼拥抱颈部。

normal.en: Compare collar, the band that sits on the neck.
normal.cn: 类比 collar，戴在颈上的衣领。

normal.en: The double c plus single l spelling is worth noting.
normal.cn: 注意双 c 加单 l 的拼写。

normal.en: It is usually plural in news style: accolades.
normal.cn: 新闻语体中常用复数 accolades。

normal.en: The highest accolade means the top honour.
normal.cn: the highest accolade 意为最高荣誉。

abstract.en: Picture a sword touching each shoulder of a kneeling man.
abstract.cn: 想象剑轻触跪者双肩。

abstract.en: Picture a golden cup raised into flashing lights.
abstract.cn: 想象金杯在闪光灯中高举。

abstract.en: Picture an audience rising as one name is read aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被念出时全场起立。

examples.en: The film swept the festival, collecting accolade after accolade.
examples.cn: 这部影片横扫电影节，斩获一项项荣誉。

examples.en: Critics gave the album their warmest accolade of the year.
examples.cn: 评论家把年度最热烈的赞誉给了这张专辑。

examples.en: In medieval courts the accolade was a ritual touch of the sword.
examples.cn: 在中世纪宫廷，册封礼是用剑轻触的仪式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克乐得」——拿奖乐得不行，就是荣誉降临。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ collum（颈）→ accolade（环颈拥抱）→ 古法语册封礼拥抱 → 英语 accolade（册封礼；引申为荣誉嘉奖）

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the medieval neck-embrace ritual to any public honour or praise.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从中世纪的环颈拥抱仪式，扩展到任何公开荣誉或赞誉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands or steel laid on the shoulders to honour
core.cn: 核心意象：以手或剑按在肩颈处以示授荣

branches.en: The original ritual on the neck of a new knight.
branches.cn: 原本施加于新骑士颈肩的仪式。

branches.en: Awards and applause standing in for that touch.
branches.cn: 奖杯与掌声替代了那一下触碰。

branches.en: Both are formal acts that mark someone chosen.
branches.cn: 两者都是标记「被选中者」的正式行为。

branches.en: Critics and festivals hand out modern accolades.
branches.cn: 评论界与电影节颁发现代的荣誉。

branches.en: History keeps the literal sense in armour scenes.
branches.cn: 历史语境保留其字面义于盔甲场景。

intro.en: The word joins the toward-prefix with the neck stem and a noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由「向」前缀、「颈」词干与名词结尾组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin collum and accolade are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the noun and the stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 collum 与 accolade 是直接祖先，拉丁条目记录名词与词干。

definition_zh: 容纳；为……提供住处；顾及；使适应
definition_en: to provide room or lodging for, to have space for, or to adjust to someone's needs
core_image: 把原本放不下的东西挪一挪，硬是留出一个位置
scene: 小礼堂原本只摆得下五十把椅子，会务组把椅子挪紧些，又多塞了二十把。The hall can accommodate seventy guests.
sceneCN: 这里 accommodate 是「容纳」（第 1 个义项：有空间装下）；句意为这个大厅能容纳七十位客人。

pos.zh: 容纳；提供住处；顾及；使适应

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「住处；调适」
由本词加现在分词后缀构成，义为「乐于助人的、通融的」

senses.title: To provide room or lodging
senses.definition: to give someone a place to stay or sit
senses.definitionCN: 给某人提供住或坐的地方
senses.example: The hostel can accommodate forty students.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅舍能接待四十名学生。
senses.why: Latin accommodare meant 'to fit one thing to another'; providing a bed means fitting a person into a place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accommodare 意为「使一物合于另一物」；提供床铺就是把一个人安置进一个地方。

senses.title: To have space for
senses.definition: of a room, vehicle, or container, to hold a certain number or amount
senses.definitionCN: 指房间、车辆或容器能装下一定数量
senses.example: The new stadium accommodates twice as many spectators.
senses.exampleCN: 新体育场能容纳两倍观众。
senses.why: Here the fitting is measured: capacity is the largest number that can be fitted without strain.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「合」是可量化的：容量就是在不勉强的前提下能装下的最大数目。

senses.title: To take account of needs
senses.definition: to adjust arrangements so that someone's needs are met
senses.definitionCN: 调整安排以满足某人的需要
senses.example: The timetable was changed to accommodate working parents.
senses.exampleCN: 时间表被调整以照顾在职父母。
senses.why: Fitting a thing to a person becomes social courtesy: schedules and rules bend so that a need can be met.
senses.whyCN: 把事物合于人就变成社会性的体贴：时间表与规则弯一弯，以满足一项需要。

senses.title: To adapt oneself
senses.definition: to adjust one's behaviour or body to a new condition
senses.definitionCN: 调整行为或身体以适应新条件
senses.example: The eye accommodates to dim light within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛在几分钟内适应昏暗光线。
senses.why: The reflexive form keeps the Latin core plainly: the see-er fits itself to what is seen.
senses.whyCN: 反身用法清楚保留拉丁核心：观看者使自己合于所见之物。

intro.en: Accommodate comes from Latin accommodare, 'to fit to', from ad- and commodus, 'fitting, suitable'.
intro.cn: accommodate 来自拉丁语 accommodare（使合于），由 ad- 与 commodus（合适的）构成。

items.en: modus meant 'measure', the root of mode and moderate.
items.cn: modus 意为「尺度」，是 mode 与 moderate 的词根。

items.en: commodus meant 'fitting, convenient', literally 'with due measure'.
items.cn: commodus 意为「合宜的、方便的」，字面是「合乎尺度」。

items.en: accommodare meant 'to fit one thing to another'.
items.cn: accommodare 意为「使一物合于另一物」。

items.en: accommodatio named the act of fitting or adjusting.
items.cn: accommodatio 指使之相合或调适的动作。

items.en: French accommoder extended the verb to lodging guests.
items.cn: 法语 accommoder 把动词扩展到安置客人。

items.en: English accommodate first meant to fit or suit, then to lodge.
items.cn: 英语 accommodate 先指使适合，后指提供住处。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun and the adjective; the second gathers verbs for holding and adjusting.
note.cn: 第一组收名词与形容词；第二组收表示容纳与调适的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for lodging or for an adjustment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住处」或「调适」。

entries.definition: An adjective for a helpful, flexible person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「乐于助人的、通融的」。

entries.definition: A formal adjective meaning roomy and convenient.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，正式用法，义为「宽敞便利的」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to contain or have capacity for.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容纳」，有容量装下。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to provide a place for people or things.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「安置、收容」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to change to suit conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使适应」。

entries.definition: A phrasal verb meaning to provide for needs.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「满足需要、提供所需」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin 'fit to' core and the capacity phrases; the abstract hooks picture chairs squeezed to make one more row.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁语「使合」核心与容量搭配；抽象记忆点想象椅子挤紧多出一排。

normal.en: Accommodate is 'fit to': Latin commodus means suitable.
normal.cn: accommodate 是「使合」：拉丁语 commodus 意为合适的。

normal.en: Accommodate guests and accommodate up to are the common patterns.
normal.cn: accommodate guests 与 accommodate up to 是常见结构。

normal.en: The noun is accommodation, with double m in both words.
normal.cn: 名词是 accommodation，两个词都双写 m。

normal.en: An accommodating person bends to help others.
normal.cn: an accommodating person 指愿意通融帮助别人的人。

normal.en: The verb covers rooms, capacity, needs, and the eye's adjustment.
normal.cn: 这个动词覆盖房间、容量、需求与眼睛的调适。

abstract.en: Picture chairs squeezed tighter so another row fits.
abstract.cn: 想象椅子挤紧以多放一排。

abstract.en: Picture a host moving furniture to make a bed for a guest.
abstract.cn: 想象主人挪家具给客人腾出床铺。

abstract.en: Picture an eye's pupil widening in a dim room.
abstract.cn: 想象昏暗房间里瞳孔放大。

examples.en: The hotel accommodates up to three hundred guests.
examples.cn: 这家旅馆最多可接待三百位客人。

examples.en: We rearranged the schedule to accommodate her treatment.
examples.cn: 我们重排日程以顾及她的治疗。

examples.en: Some animals accommodate quickly to changes in temperature.
examples.cn: 有些动物能迅速适应温度变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿科莫代特」——把东西挪一挪、合进去，就是容纳与照顾。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ modus（尺度）→ commodus（合宜的）→ accommodare（使合）；核心义是「把一方安置进另一方的尺度里」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from giving someone a place, to measuring capacity, to bending arrangements for a need, to a body adjusting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从给某人一个位置，走到测量容量，再到为需求调整安排，最后是身体自我调适。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shifting things until one more fits in
core.cn: 核心意象：挪动物件直到多出一个位置

branches.en: A place found for a person to stay or sit.
branches.cn: 为某人找到住或坐的地方。

branches.en: A measured limit of how much fits.
branches.cn: 能容纳多少的量度上限。

branches.en: Arrangements bent to meet someone's need.
branches.cn: 为满足某人需求而调整的安排。

branches.en: A body fitting itself to new conditions.
branches.cn: 身体使自己适应新条件。

branches.en: Providing room and measuring room share the same fitting image.
branches.cn: 提供位置与测量容量共享同一个「合」的意象。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin prefix ad- with the measure root mod-, and its family adds the action noun and participle adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与「尺度」词根 mod- 结合，词族另加动作名词与分词形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin accommodare and accommodatio are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the verb and its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accommodare 与 accommodatio 是直接祖先，因此拉丁条目记录动词与其名词。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「住处；调适」
形容词，义为「乐于助人的、通融的」

definition_zh: 伴奏；伴随物；佐餐之物
definition_en: music played along with a singer or player, or something that goes together with something else
core_image: 钢琴旁的陪奏：主旋律在前，和声托底
scene: 音乐厅里琴声轻起，托着她的歌声缓缓升起来。The pianist played a soft accompaniment for the singer.
sceneCN: 这里 accompaniment 是「伴奏」（第 1 个义项：托举主唱或主奏的音乐）；句意为钢琴家为歌手奏出轻柔的伴奏。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「陪伴；为……伴奏」
由本词加施动后缀构成，义为「伴奏者」
由动词加现在分词后缀构成，义为「伴随的」

senses.title: Music under a lead performer
senses.definition: music played to support a singer or a main instrument
senses.definitionCN: 为歌手或主奏乐器提供支撑的音乐
senses.example: The cellist added a rich accompaniment to the aria.
senses.exampleCN: 大提琴手为咏叹调增添了丰厚的伴奏。
senses.why: The verb accompany means to go along with someone, and music that walks beside a voice keeps that image.
senses.whyCN: 动词 accompany 意为陪伴某人，托在歌声旁行走的音乐正保留了这一意象。

senses.title: A thing that goes along with another
senses.definition: something that naturally appears together with something else
senses.definitionCN: 自然而然与另一物相伴出现的东西
senses.example: Rain is a familiar accompaniment to the monsoon.
senses.exampleCN: 雨是季风常见的伴随物。
senses.why: Whatever habitually walks beside a thing, in food or in weather, borrows the music image of supporting from the side.
senses.whyCN: 凡惯常伴于一物之侧的东西——无论是佐餐还是天气——都借用了「从旁托举」的音乐意象。

intro.en: Accompaniment comes from accompany plus the noun suffix -ment, from Late Latin companio, 'one who shares bread'.
intro.cn: accompaniment 由 accompany 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，其远源是后期拉丁语 companio（分食面包的人）。

items.en: companio meant one who shares bread with you, panis being bread.
items.cn: companio 意为与你分享面包（panis）的人。

items.en: compaignon meant companion, one who walks with you.
items.cn: 古法语 compaignon 意为同行者、伙伴。

items.en: companion entered English for a person who goes along.
items.cn: companion 进入英语，指同行之人。

items.en: The verb accompany meant to go along with, later to play along.
items.cn: 动词 accompany 意为伴随，后指配乐陪奏。

items.en: Adding -ment made the noun for the act or music of accompanying.
items.cn: 加后缀 -ment 构成名词，指伴奏或伴随行为。

note.en: The first group gathers the companion word family; the second gathers words for backing music and pairings.
note.cn: 第一组收 companion 词族；第二组收表示陪衬音乐或搭配的词。

entries.definition: The person who plays the accompaniment.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指伴奏者。

entries.definition: The base verb of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同根动词，本词的基础。

entries.definition: A partner in wrongdoing; spelling-similar, different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指同谋犯；仅拼写相近，来源不同。

entries.definition: Informal music supporting a main singer.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，口语指伴唱配乐。

entries.definition: Independent melody set against another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指与主旋律相对的独立声部。

entries.definition: Something that completes or suits another thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补足物；相配之物」。

entries.definition: Food served along with the main dish.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，指随主菜一起上桌的配菜。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the bread-sharing root and the -ment suffix; the abstract hooks picture piano under voice.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「分面包」词根与 -ment 后缀；抽象记忆点想象钢琴托着歌声。

normal.en: The root panis means bread: companions once shared bread.
normal.cn: 词根 panis 意为面包：同伴本是分面包的人。

normal.en: Accompaniment is accompany plus -ment.
normal.cn: accompaniment 即 accompany 加 -ment。

normal.en: In music it is the part that supports the lead.
normal.cn: 在音乐中，它指支撑主声部的部分。

normal.en: Without accompaniment means singing alone, unaccompanied.
normal.cn: without accompaniment 即无伴奏清唱。

normal.en: Food writers use it for side dishes that suit a main dish.
normal.cn: 美食作者用它指与主菜相配的佐餐物。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow that follows every step of a dancer.
abstract.cn: 想象紧随舞者每一步的影子。

abstract.en: Picture bread broken between two friends walking together.
abstract.cn: 想象同行友人之间掰开的面包。

abstract.en: Picture rice quietly carrying the taste of a rich sauce.
abstract.cn: 想象米饭静静托起浓酱的滋味。

examples.en: The choir sang to a simple guitar accompaniment.
examples.cn: 合唱团在简单的吉他伴奏下演唱。

examples.en: Storms arrived in accompaniment with the first cold front.
examples.cn: 风暴伴随第一股冷空气一同到来。

examples.en: A crisp salad makes a fine accompaniment to grilled fish.
examples.cn: 爽脆的沙拉是烤鱼的绝佳搭配。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿坎帕尼门特」——同伴（companion）站在门（ment）边陪你演奏，就是伴奏。

root: 拉丁语 com-（共同）+ panis（面包）→ companio（共食者）→ companion → accompany（陪伴）+ -ment → accompaniment（伴奏；伴随物）

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from music that supports a performer, to anything that habitually goes along with another.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从支撑表演者的音乐，扩展到惯常伴随他物的一切。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one thing walking beside another, quietly supporting
core.cn: 核心意象：一物伴于另一物之侧，静默支撑

branches.en: Music that walks beside a voice or lead line.
branches.cn: 伴于歌声或主旋律旁行走的音乐。

branches.en: Rain, sauce, or friendship that habitually pairs with something.
branches.cn: 惯常与某物成对的雨、酱汁或友谊。

branches.en: Both senses keep the side-by-side picture.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留并肩而行的画面。

branches.en: The support must stay secondary to the lead.
branches.cn: 伴奏必须居于主声部之下。

branches.en: The pairing feels natural, almost inevitable.
branches.cn: 这种配对显得自然，近乎必然。

intro.en: The word is the verb accompany plus the act-noun suffix -ment; the family adds an agent noun.
intro.cn: 这个词是动词 accompany 加行为名词后缀 -ment；词族另派生施动名词。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin companio is the deep ancestor, so the Latin entry records the bread-sharing word.
latinIntro.cn: 后期拉丁语 companio 是深远祖先，拉丁条目记录这个「分面包」的词。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「陪伴；伴奏」

definition_zh: 伴奏者；伴奏员
definition_en: a musician who plays music to support a singer or another performer
core_image: 琴凳上的托举者：让主唱站上光亮的中心
scene: 彩排室里她翻着乐谱，目光始终追着歌手的呼吸。The rehearsal pianist served as the choir's accompanist for ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 accompanist 是「伴奏者」（第 1 个义项：为他人演奏托举性音乐的人）；句意为这位排练钢琴师担任合唱团伴奏十年。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「陪伴；伴奏」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「伴奏」

senses.title: A musician who supports another performer
senses.definition: a player, often a pianist, who provides the supporting music for a lead performer
senses.definitionCN: 为领唱或主奏者提供支撑音乐的乐手，常为钢琴师
senses.example: The accompanist followed the singer's every pause.
senses.exampleCN: 伴奏者紧随着歌手的每一次停顿。
senses.why: The suffix -ist names a person who does the act, so the word names the one who plays the accompaniment.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ist 标记做某一行为的人，所以这个词指演奏伴奏的人。

senses.title: A helpful partner in music-making
senses.definition: any musician who supports the ensemble, such as a rehearsal pianist for a choir or a dance class
senses.definitionCN: 泛指支撑整个排演的音乐家，如为合唱团、舞蹈课弹伴奏的排练琴师
senses.example: The dance school hired a full-time accompanist last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所舞蹈学校去年聘请了全职伴奏。
senses.why: Beyond the concert stage, anyone whose art is playing under others, in studios and classrooms, earns the same name.
senses.whyCN: 走出音乐厅，凡在琴房与教室里以托举他人为艺的乐手，都配得上这个称谓。

intro.en: Accompanist adds the person suffix -ist to accompany, whose Latin root companio meant one who shares bread.
intro.cn: accompanist 在 accompany 之上加「人」后缀 -ist，其拉丁词根 companio 意为分食面包的人。

items.en: companio meant one who shares bread, panis being bread.
items.cn: companio 意为分享面包之人，panis 即面包。

items.en: compaignon meant one who travels with another.
items.cn: 古法语 compaignon 意为同行者。

items.en: The verb meant to go along with, later to play along with.
items.cn: 动词意为伴随，后指配乐陪奏。

items.en: French used accompanateur for the supporting player.
items.cn: 法语用 accompanateur 指伴奏乐手。

items.en: English formed accompanist with its own -ist suffix.
items.cn: 英语用自有的 -ist 后缀造出 accompanist。

note.en: The first group gathers the companion word family; the second gathers names for supporting musicians.
note.cn: 第一组收 companion 词族；第二组收指辅助乐手的称谓。

entries.definition: The music the accompanist plays.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指伴奏者奏出的音乐。

entries.definition: The base verb of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 同根动词，词族的基础。

entries.definition: A partner in crime; spelling-similar, different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指同谋；仅拼写相近，来源不同。

entries.definition: A longer phrase for the same role.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，指同一角色的较长说法。

entries.definition: A band member supporting the lead, in jazz usage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，爵士乐用语，指辅助主奏的乐手。

entries.definition: The featured performer the accompanist supports.
entries.definitionCN: 对照名词，指伴奏者所托举的主奏者。

entries.definition: One who directs rather than accompanies a choir.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指指挥而非伴奏合唱团的人。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -ist person suffix and the shared-bread root; the abstract hooks picture the patient player.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「人」后缀 -ist 与「分面包」词根；抽象记忆点想象耐心的琴师。

normal.en: -ist marks a person: accompanist is the one who accompanies.
normal.cn: -ist 标记人：accompanist 就是做伴奏的人。

normal.en: Compare artist and violinist for the same pattern.
normal.cn: 类比 artist、violinist，同一构词模式。

normal.en: The word hides accompany plus the -ist tail.
normal.cn: 词内藏着 accompany 加 -ist 尾。

normal.en: Most accompanists are pianists in practice.
normal.cn: 实践中伴奏者多为钢琴师。

normal.en: The plural is accompanists.
normal.cn: 复数为 accompanists。

abstract.en: Picture a pianist watching the singer, not the keys.
abstract.cn: 想象盯着歌手而非琴键的琴师。

abstract.en: Picture a helper lifting a friend onto a stage.
abstract.cn: 想象把友人托上舞台的帮手。

abstract.en: Picture bread shared quietly before the concert begins.
abstract.cn: 想象音乐会开场前静静分享的面包。

examples.en: The young accompanist sight-read the entire sonata without error.
examples.cn: 年轻的伴奏者毫无差错地视奏了整首奏鸣曲。

examples.en: Every competitor may bring a personal accompanist.
examples.cn: 每位选手都可以自带伴奏。

examples.en: A good accompanist listens more than plays.
examples.cn: 优秀的伴奏者听多于奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿坎帕尼斯特」——同伴里最「斯特」（厉害）的那个，专门为别人伴奏。

root: 拉丁语 com-（共同）+ panis（面包）→ companio → accompany（伴奏）+ -ist（人）→ accompanist（伴奏者）

sensesIntro.en: The word has one focused sense: the musician whose art is supporting another performer.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词义项集中：指以托举他人表演为艺的乐手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the player who makes someone else shine
core.cn: 核心意象：让别人发光的演奏者

branches.en: The pianist or player under the lead performer.
branches.cn: 居于主唱主奏之下的琴师或乐手。

branches.en: Choosing to stay in the shadow by choice.
branches.cn: 甘愿退居暗影的选择。

branches.en: Listening is the first skill of this person.
branches.cn: 倾听是这种人的第一技艺。

branches.en: The role completes the performance rather than rivals it.
branches.cn: 这个角色成全演出而非与之争锋。

branches.en: The shared-bread origin keeps the humble partnership alive.
branches.cn: 「分面包」的词源让谦逊的伙伴关系延续至今。

intro.en: The word joins the accompany stem with the person suffix -ist.
intro.cn: 这个词由 accompany 词干加「人」后缀 -ist 构成。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin companio is the deep root, so the Latin entry records the bread-sharing word.
latinIntro.cn: 后期拉丁语 companio 是深远词根，拉丁条目记录这个「分面包」的词。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「陪伴；伴奏」
名词，义为「伴奏」

definition_zh: 陪伴；陪同；伴随；附有；配餐；伴奏；自弹自唱
definition_en: to go somewhere with someone, to happen or exist together with something, or to play music in support of a performer
core_image: 两个人并排走，一个人的步子跟着另一个人的步子
scene: 演出前的后台很安静，歌手在钢琴边等灯光亮起。A young pianist accompanied her on the old upright piano.
sceneCN: 这里 accompany 指「为演唱者伴奏」（第 6 个义项：用乐器为表演者伴奏）；句意为一位年轻钢琴手用那架旧立式钢琴为她伴奏。

pos.zh: 动词：陪伴；陪同；伴随；附有；伴奏

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「伴奏；伴随物」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「伴奏者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「附随的；同时发生的」
由否定前缀 un- 加过去分词构成，义为「无人陪同的；无伴奏的」

senses.title: To go somewhere with someone
senses.definition: to travel or go somewhere together with another person, as a companion
senses.definitionCN: 指作为同伴与另一个人一起走或去某处
senses.example: Her brother accompanied her to the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 她哥哥陪她去了机场。
senses.why: The Latin word began as 'one who shares bread'; sharing the road grows straight out of sharing a meal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词原本指「一起分面包的人」；一起分过面包，就很自然地走到一起上路。

senses.title: To escort someone politely
senses.definition: to go with someone to a place or to the door, especially in order to be polite or to protect them
senses.definitionCN: 指陪某人走到某处或门口，尤指出于礼貌或保护
senses.example: The host accompanied us to the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 主人把我们送到大门口。
senses.why: A companion who walks a guest out turns the shared road into a small act of courtesy.
senses.whyCN: 陪客人走出去的同伴，把「共走一段路」变成了一种小小的礼节。

senses.title: To happen at the same time as
senses.definition: of an event, condition, or symptom, to occur together with something else
senses.definitionCN: 指事件、状况或症状与另一事物同时出现
senses.example: The fever is often accompanied by a sore throat.
senses.exampleCN: 发烧常常伴有喉咙痛。
senses.why: Walking together becomes happening together: two things keep the same pace without either one causing the other.
senses.whyCN: 「一起走」变成「一起发生」：两件事步调一致，但谁也不必然引起谁。

senses.title: To be supplied together with
senses.definition: of a document, object, or item, to be provided together with something else
senses.definitionCN: 指文件、物品或附件与另一事物一起提供
senses.example: The application must be accompanied by two photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 申请材料必须附上两张照片。
senses.why: The thing that travels with the main thing is a companion in the literal sense: it never arrives alone.
senses.whyCN: 与主体一起走的东西就是字面意义上的同伴：它从不单独到达。

senses.title: To be served with a food or drink
senses.definition: of a drink or dish, to be served together with a particular food because the two go well together
senses.definitionCN: 指某种饮料或菜肴与特定食物搭配供应，因为二者相配
senses.example: A light white wine accompanies the fish course.
senses.exampleCN: 这道鱼配一款清淡的白葡萄酒。
senses.why: At the table the companion is the dish or drink that keeps the main course company.
senses.whyCN: 在餐桌上，同伴就是陪着主菜的那道菜或那杯酒。

senses.title: To play music in support of a performer
senses.definition: to play an instrument while someone sings or plays the main part
senses.definitionCN: 指在别人演唱或演奏主旋律时用乐器伴奏
senses.example: A young pianist accompanied her on the old upright piano.
senses.exampleCN: 一位年轻钢琴手用那架旧立式钢琴为她伴奏。
senses.why: In music the supporter literally walks beside the soloist, note for note, without taking the lead.
senses.whyCN: 在音乐里，支持者确实与独奏者并肩而行，一个音一个音地跟着，却不抢主位。

senses.title: To accompany oneself
senses.definition: in the phrase accompany oneself, to sing while playing an instrument for one's own support
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 accompany oneself，指一边演唱一边用乐器为自己伴奏
senses.example: He accompanied himself on the guitar at the small bar.
senses.exampleCN: 他在小酒吧里抱着吉他自弹自唱。
senses.why: The companion and the soloist collapse into one person, but the two roles stay separate in the grammar.
senses.whyCN: 同伴与独唱者合成了一个人，但这两个角色在语法上仍然分开。

senses.title: To add a gesture alongside words
senses.definition: to do something at the same time as speaking or acting, so that the two support each other
senses.definitionCN: 指在说话或行动的同时做另一件事，使二者互相配合
senses.example: He accompanied the warning with a shake of his head.
senses.exampleCN: 他一边警告，一边摇了摇头。
senses.why: Any action that walks beside another action is a companion; a gesture can accompany a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 任何与另一动作并肩而行的动作都是同伴；一个手势可以陪伴一句话。

intro.en: Accompany goes back to a Latin phrase for sharing bread, and the word still means keeping someone company.
intro.cn: accompany 可追溯到拉丁语中「分面包」的说法，这个词至今仍表示与人为伴。

items.en: Panis meant 'bread'; it is generally connected with pascere 'to feed, graze', though the deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: panis 意为「面包」；一般认为与 pascere「喂养、放牧」有关，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Com- 'with' plus panis formed companio, 'one who shares bread with another'.
items.cn: com-「与」加 panis 构成 companio，意为「与他人分面包的人」。

items.en: Old French compaign meant 'companion', and the verb acompaignier meant 'to join someone as a companion'.
items.cn: 古法语 compaign 意为「同伴」，动词 acompaignier 意为「作为同伴加入某人」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century; the musical sense is recorded from the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词；音乐义从十八世纪起有记录。

items.en: The passive form be accompanied by became a fixed pattern for symptoms, documents, and sounds.
items.cn: 被动形式 be accompanied by 成为描述症状、文件与声音的固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same bread root; the near-meaning group lists other ways of going along with someone.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「面包」词根的一族词；近义组列出其他「与人同行」的说法。

entries.definition: The music or thing that goes with a main part.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伴奏、伴随物」，指与主体相配的音乐或事物。

entries.definition: A musician who plays for a singer or a soloist.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伴奏者」，指为歌手或独奏者伴奏的音乐家。

entries.definition: Without anyone or anything going along; also used of music with no accompaniment.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无人陪同的、无伴奏的」，指没有同伴或没有伴奏。

entries.definition: A person who spends time with you, sharing the same bread root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同伴、伙伴」，与本词共享「面包」词根。

entries.definition: The state of being with others, or a business, also from the bread root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「陪伴、公司」，同样出自「面包」词根。

entries.definition: To go with someone to protect or guide them, more formal than accompany.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「护送、陪同」，比 accompany 更正式，带有保护或引导意味。

entries.definition: To go with someone as a servant or official helper, an old formal use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「随行、侍候」，是很旧的正式用法，指作为随从或助手同行。

entries.definition: To travel with vehicles or ships in order to protect them.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「护送、护航」，指为车辆或船只护行。

entries.definition: To go with young people to keep them safe and well behaved.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「陪同监护」，指陪着年轻人以保证安全与规矩。

entries.definition: To play music behind a singer, an informal word for the musical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「为……伴奏、在背后支持」，是音乐义的口语说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real bread root and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的「面包」词根，以及这个词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: panis is bread: a companion is someone you share bread with.
normal.cn: panis 是「面包」：companion 就是和你分面包的人。

normal.en: The same root gives companion, company and companionship.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 companion、company 与 companionship。

normal.en: To accompany someone is to keep them company on the road.
normal.cn: to accompany someone 就是在路上与某人作伴。

normal.en: Be accompanied by is the pattern for symptoms and documents.
normal.cn: be accompanied by 是症状与文件常用的句式。

normal.en: An accompanist is the player who walks beside the soloist.
normal.cn: accompanist 就是走在独奏者身旁的演奏者。

abstract.en: Two pairs of footprints in the same snow, one set always half a step behind.
abstract.cn: 同一片雪地上有两行脚印，其中一行总落后半步。

abstract.en: A companion can be a person, a fever, a photograph or a chord; what matters is that it never arrives alone.
abstract.cn: 同伴可以是一个人、一场发烧、一张照片或一个和弦；关键在于它从不单独到来。

abstract.en: To accompany is to lend your step to someone else's direction.
abstract.cn: 陪伴就是把自己的脚步借给别人的方向。

examples.en: Her brother accompanied her to the airport.
examples.cn: 她哥哥陪她去了机场。

examples.en: The fever is often accompanied by a sore throat.
examples.cn: 发烧常常伴有喉咙痛。

examples.en: He accompanied himself on the guitar at the small bar.
examples.cn: 他在小酒吧里抱着吉他自弹自唱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康帕尼」——两个人并排走，一个跟着一个的步子：陪伴、伴奏。

root: 晚期拉丁语 companio「分面包的人」由 com-「与」加 panis「面包」构成；古法语 acompaignier「作伴」进入英语成为 accompany。更早的印欧词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Accompany begins with two people sharing bread and walking the same road, then spreads to symptoms, documents, dishes, music, and even a gesture that follows a sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: accompany 从两个人分面包、同走一条路开始，随后扩展到症状、文件、菜肴、音乐，甚至扩展到跟着一句话出现的手势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people walk side by side, one step keeping time with the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人并排走，一个人的步子跟着另一个人的步子。

branches.en: THE PERSON: walking beside a friend, or politely seeing a guest out.
branches.cn: 人物线：走在朋友身旁，或礼貌地把客人送出门。

branches.en: THE EVENT: two things keep pace, such as a fever and a sore throat.
branches.cn: 事件线：两件事步调一致，例如发烧与喉咙痛。

branches.en: THE THING: the photograph with an application and the wine with a fish course.
branches.cn: 物品线：随申请附上的照片，以及配鱼的葡萄酒。

branches.en: THE MUSIC: a pianist beside a singer, or a singer playing for himself.
branches.cn: 音乐线：歌手身旁的钢琴手，或自己为自己弹唱的歌手。

branches.en: THE GESTURE: a shake of the head that goes along with a warning.
branches.cn: 动作线：跟着一句警告一起出现的摇头。

intro.en: Accompany entered English as a French verb, and English added familiar endings to build the family.
intro.cn: accompany 作为法语动词进入英语，英语再加上常见的后缀扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun panis and the Late Latin companio are recorded; the compound is transparent, the deeper root is not.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 panis 与晚期拉丁语 companio 均有记录；复合结构清楚，更早的词根则不清楚。

items.meaning: to join someone as a companion

items.exampleCN: panis 是表示「面包」的词根。
companio 产生了英语的 companion。

items.meaning: a person who keeps you company
items.example: The dog was his only companion.
items.exampleCN: 那只狗是他唯一的伙伴。

derivatives.zh: 伴奏；伴随物
伴奏者
附随的；同时发生的
无人陪同的；无伴奏的

definition_zh: 共犯；帮凶；同伙
definition_en: a person who helps another person commit a crime
core_image: 一个人动手，另一个人在门口望风
scene: 监控里看到，进店偷东西的只有一人，但门外有人不断打手势提醒时间。Police later arrested his accomplice.
sceneCN: 这里 accomplice 是「共犯、帮凶」（第 1 个义项：协助他人犯罪者）；句意为警方后来逮捕了他的同伙。

derivatives.zh: 同源动词，义为「陪同」，语义上指同行之人
形近但不同源，义为「完成」

senses.title: A helper in a crime
senses.definition: a person who knowingly helps another to commit an offence
senses.definitionCN: 明知而协助他人实施犯罪的人
senses.example: The driver was charged as an accomplice in the escape.
senses.exampleCN: 司机作为逃跑帮凶被起诉。
senses.why: The word grew from complice, 'one joined with another'; in law that joining is a partnership in wrongdoing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 complice（与他人联结者）演变而来；法律上这种联结就是共同作恶的伙伴关系。

senses.title: A partner in mischief
senses.definition: a person who joins another in a mischievous or foolish act, without legal seriousness
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起做淘气或愚蠢之事者，不含法律严重性
senses.example: Her little brother was her accomplice in hiding the cake.
senses.exampleCN: 她弟弟是她藏蛋糕的同伙。
senses.why: Outside law, the word's 'partner' frame survives in jokes: the partner shares the scheme, if not the crime.
senses.whyCN: 在法律之外，这个词的「伙伴」框架残存在玩笑中：伙伴分担的是主意，未必是罪。

intro.en: Accomplice comes from Old French complice, reshaped by association with accomplish; both trace to Latin complere, 'to fill up'.
intro.cn: accomplice 来自古法语 complice，因与 accomplish 联想而被改写；二者都可追到拉丁语 complere（填满）。

items.en: complere meant 'to fill up, complete', from com- and plere 'to fill'.
items.cn: complere 意为「填满、完成」，由 com- 与 plere（填）构成。

items.en: complex meant 'woven together, closely connected'.
items.cn: complex 意为「交织在一起、紧密关联的」。

items.en: complice meant an associate or partner in a matter.
items.cn: complice 指某事中的同伙或伙伴。

items.en: English borrowed complice, then inserted an a by confusion with accomplish.
items.cn: 英语借入 complice，后因与 accomplish 混淆而插入 a。

items.en: Criminal law fixed accomplice for a person who aids an offence.
items.cn: 刑法固定 accomplice 指协助犯罪者。

items.en: Modern usage keeps the legal sense and a lighter playful one.
items.cn: 现代用法保留法律义与较轻的戏谑义。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alikes often confused with it; the second gathers words for a partner in wrongdoing.
note.cn: 第一组收易混的近形词；第二组收表示共同作恶者的词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to complete a task successfully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「完成、实现」。

entries.definition: An adjective for a highly skilled person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「技艺高超的」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to go with someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「陪同」，与 accomplice 非同源。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning obedient to rules.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「顺从的、合规的」。

entries.definition: A general word for a person working with another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伙伴」，泛指与他人合作者。

entries.definition: A legal term for a person who assists a crime.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，法律用语，义为「从犯」。

entries.definition: A person joined with others in a plot.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同谋者」，参与密谋者。

entries.definition: A loyal follower who carries out another's plans.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「亲信、打手」，执行他人计划者。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the inserted-a story and the police phrases; the abstract hooks picture one thief inside and one watcher outside.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「插入 a」的拼写故事与警务搭配；抽象记忆点想象一人店内行窃、一人在外望风。

normal.en: Accomplice looks like accomplish, but it means a partner in crime.
normal.cn: accomplice 看起来像 accomplish，却指犯罪同伙。

normal.en: The a was inserted by confusion with accomplish.
normal.cn: 那个 a 是因与 accomplish 混淆而插入的。

normal.en: An accomplice to the crime is the standard legal phrase.
normal.cn: an accomplice to the crime 是标准法律短语。

normal.en: The plural is accomplices, keeping the c soft.
normal.cn: 复数是 accomplices，c 仍读软音。

normal.en: In law, accomplice and accessory are distinct roles.
normal.cn: 法律上 accomplice 与 accessory 是不同角色。

abstract.en: Picture one person inside a shop and one watching the street.
abstract.cn: 想象一人在店内、一人在街上望风。

abstract.en: Picture two children hiding a cake in a cupboard.
abstract.cn: 想象两个孩子把蛋糕藏进橱柜。

abstract.en: Picture a driver waiting with the engine running.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车开着引擎等待。

examples.en: She was convicted as an accomplice in the fraud.
examples.cn: 她作为诈骗案共犯被定罪。

examples.en: The robber's accomplice waited in the car.
examples.cn: 劫匪的同伙在车里等候。

examples.en: His accomplice in the prank was the quietest boy in class.
examples.cn: 他搞恶作剧的同伙是班上最安静的男孩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康普利斯」——一个人动手，另一个人在门口打手势，就是帮凶。

root: 拉丁语 com-（一起）+ plere（填）→ complex（交织）→ 古法语 complice；核心义是「与他人绑在同一件事上的人」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the legal partner in a crime, to the lighter partner in mischief.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从法律上的犯罪同伙，走到较轻的恶作剧同伙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person acts while another stands watch
core.cn: 核心意象：一人行动，另一人望风

branches.en: A person who knowingly aids an offence.
branches.cn: 明知而协助犯罪者。

branches.en: A partner in a harmless prank.
branches.cn: 无害恶作剧中的伙伴。

branches.en: Both senses rest on a shared scheme.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在共同的谋划上。

branches.en: The legal word and the playful word are one frame with different weights.
branches.cn: 法律词与戏谑词是同一框架的不同分量。

branches.en: A partner's role ranges from watching to sharing the blame.
branches.cn: 伙伴的角色从望风到分担罪责。

intro.en: The word keeps a Latin 'together' prefix and a filling root, with the -ice ending marking a person.
intro.cn: 这个词保留拉丁语「一起」前缀与「填」词根，并以 -ice 后缀指人。

latinIntro.en: Latin complex and the French form complice are the ancestors, so the Latin entries record the root and the derived adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 complex 与法语形式 complice 是祖先，因此拉丁条目记录词根与派生形容词。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「陪同」（同源，指同行之人）
名词，义为「同谋、串通」

definition_zh: 完成；实现；达到
definition_en: to succeed in doing or completing something planned
core_image: 清单上最后一项被划掉，笔尖停住
scene: 他花了三个月修补旧钟，最后一个齿轮咬合时，秒针重新走了起来。They accomplished the repair without new parts.
sceneCN: 这里 accomplish 是「完成」（第 1 个义项：把计划中的事做完）；句意为他们没有用新零件就完成了修理。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「成就；完成」
由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「技艺高超的」

senses.title: To complete a task
senses.definition: to carry out a piece of work until it is finished
senses.definitionCN: 把一项工作做到结束
senses.example: The team accomplished the survey in two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 团队用两周完成了这次调查。
senses.why: Latin complere meant 'to fill up'; accomplish adds ad- and keeps the image of filling a task until nothing is missing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 complere 意为「填满」；accomplish 加上 ad-，保留「把任务填满、不留缺口」的意象。

senses.title: To achieve an aim
senses.definition: to succeed in reaching something intended or desired
senses.definitionCN: 成功达到意图或期望之物
senses.example: They accomplished more than anyone expected.
senses.exampleCN: 他们取得的成果超出所有人的预期。
senses.why: The filled measure can be a goal rather than a task: the aim is reached and nothing remains to be done.
senses.whyCN: 被填满的尺度也可以是目标而非任务：目的达到，再无未竟之事。

senses.title: To bring to full development
senses.definition: in older use, to complete a person's training or a design's quality
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法中，完成一个人的训练或使设计达到完善
senses.example: Years of practice accomplished him as a violinist.
senses.exampleCN: 多年练习把他造就成一名小提琴手。
senses.why: This older sense survives mainly in the adjective accomplished, where completion means polished skill.
senses.whyCN: 这一旧义主要残存在形容词 accomplished 中，那里的「完成」意味着娴熟的技艺。

intro.en: Accomplish comes from Old French acomplir, from Latin complere, 'to fill up'.
intro.cn: accomplish 来自古法语 acomplir，源自拉丁语 complere（填满）。

items.en: plere meant 'to fill', the root of complete and supplement.
items.cn: plere 意为「填」，是 complete 与 supplement 的词根。

items.en: complere meant 'to fill up, finish'.
items.cn: complere 意为「填满、完成」。

items.en: acomplir meant 'to fulfil, carry out'.
items.cn: acomplir 意为「履行、完成」。

items.en: English accomplish first meant to complete a duty or a period.
items.cn: 英语 accomplish 最初指完成职责或一段时间。

items.en: The participle accomplished came to mean highly skilled.
items.cn: 分词 accomplished 逐渐表示技艺高超。

items.en: Modern usage concentrates on tasks and goals.
items.cn: 现代用法集中在任务与目标。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun and the participle adjective; the second gathers verbs of finishing.
note.cn: 第一组收名词与分词形容词；第二组收表示完成的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for an achievement or the act of finishing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成就」或「完成的行为」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning highly skilled.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「技艺高超的」。

entries.definition: A partner in a crime, often confused with this word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「共犯」，常与本词混淆。

entries.definition: An adjective and verb from the same Latin filling root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词与动词，同出拉丁语「填满」词根。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to reach a goal through effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「实现、达到」，经努力达到目标。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to carry out a promise or need.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「履行、满足」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to finish something begun.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「完成」，结束已开始之事。

entries.definition: A phrasal verb meaning to perform a plan or order.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「执行、实施」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'fill up' root and the task phrases; the abstract hooks picture the last box on a list being ticked.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「填满」词根与任务搭配；抽象记忆点想象清单最后一格被划掉。

normal.en: Accomplish is Latin 'fill up': complere means to fill.
normal.cn: accomplish 是拉丁语「填满」：complere 意为填。

normal.en: Accomplish a task and accomplish a goal are the two patterns.
normal.cn: accomplish a task 与 accomplish a goal 是两种搭配。

normal.en: The noun is accomplishment, the participle accomplished.
normal.cn: 名词是 accomplishment，分词是 accomplished。

normal.en: Accomplished describes a skilled musician or writer.
normal.cn: accomplished 形容技艺高超的音乐家或作家。

normal.en: Watch the ending: -ish, not -ice like accomplice.
normal.cn: 注意词尾：是 -ish，而不是 accomplice 的 -ice。

abstract.en: Picture the last box on a long checklist being ticked.
abstract.cn: 想象一长串清单上最后一格被划掉。

abstract.en: Picture a clock's last gear clicking into place.
abstract.cn: 想象钟表最后一个齿轮咔哒咬合。

abstract.en: Picture a goalpost reached after a long uphill run.
abstract.cn: 想象长坡跑后抵达球门柱。

examples.en: The crew accomplished the rescue in darkness.
examples.cn: 救援队摸黑完成了救援。

examples.en: Little was accomplished by the second meeting.
examples.cn: 第二次会议几乎没取得任何成果。

examples.en: She is an accomplished cellist as well as a doctor.
examples.cn: 她既是医生，也是一位技艺高超的大提琴手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康普利什」——把一项任务填满、填到没有缺口，就是完成。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ plere（填）→ complere（填满）→ 古法语 acomplir；核心义是「做到没有缺口」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from finishing a piece of work, to reaching an aim, to the older sense of perfecting a person's skill.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从把一件工作做完，走到达到目的，再到旧有的「使人技艺完善」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last item on a checklist crossed out
core.cn: 核心意象：清单上最后一项被划掉

branches.en: A piece of work carried to its end.
branches.cn: 被做到尽头的一项工作。

branches.en: An intended aim actually reached.
branches.cn: 真正达到的预期目的。

branches.en: A person brought to polished skill.
branches.cn: 被造就到技艺娴熟的人。

branches.en: Task and goal are two kinds of full measure.
branches.cn: 任务与目标是两种「填满」的尺度。

branches.en: Reaching a goal and perfecting a craft both end in accomplishment.
branches.cn: 达到目标与完善技艺都以成就收尾。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin prefix ad- with the filling root pl-, and its family adds the action noun and participle.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与「填」词根 pl- 结合，词族另加动作名词与分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin complere is the direct ancestor, so the Latin entries record the verb and its participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 complere 是直接祖先，因此拉丁条目记录动词与分词。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「成就；完成」
形容词，义为「技艺高超的」

definition_zh: 上前搭话；拦住（陌生人）；乞讨纠缠
definition_en: to approach and speak to someone, especially in a bold or unwanted way
core_image: 一个人从路边横跨一步，挡在行人面前开口
scene: 游客刚出车站，就有人贴上来问要不要换钱，一路跟着走了半条街。A stranger accosted him outside the station.
sceneCN: 这里 accost 是「上前搭话、拦住」（第 1 个义项：以冒失或不受欢迎的方式接近并开口）；句意为一名陌生人在车站外拦住他。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「被拦住的」
由本词加现在分词后缀构成，名词化后义为「拦截搭话的行为」

senses.title: To approach and speak boldly
senses.definition: to come up to someone and speak first, often when it is unwelcome
senses.definitionCN: 主动走到某人面前开口，且常不受欢迎
senses.example: A reporter accosted the minister at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 一名记者在入口处拦住部长提问。
senses.why: The word came through French from Latin accostare, 'to come to the side of'; the first move is physical, standing beside someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语 accostare（走到……旁边）；第一个动作是物理的，站到别人身侧。

senses.title: To solicit or beg persistently
senses.definition: to approach people repeatedly to beg, sell, or solicit
senses.definitionCN: 反复接近他人以乞讨、兜售或拉客
senses.example: He was accosted by touts at every corner of the market.
senses.exampleCN: 市场上的每个转角都有拉客者缠上他。
senses.why: When the approach comes with a demand, the neutral 'come beside' hardens into pestering, the sense most common in city scenes.
senses.whyCN: 当接近伴随索取，中性的「走到旁边」就硬化为纠缠，这是城市场景中最常见的用法。

intro.en: Accost reached English through Old French from Latin accostare, 'to come to the side of', related to costa, 'rib, side'.
intro.cn: accost 经古法语来自拉丁语 accostare（走到旁边），与 costa（肋骨、侧边）相关。

items.en: costa meant 'rib, side', the root of coast and accost.
items.cn: costa 意为「肋骨、侧边」，是 coast 与 accost 的词根。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant 'to, toward'.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「向」。

items.en: accostare meant 'to come up to the side of' someone.
items.cn: accostare 意为「走到某人旁边」。

items.en: acooster meant 'to approach, come alongside'.
items.cn: acooster 意为「接近、靠到旁边」。

items.en: English accost first meant to come alongside a ship or a person.
items.cn: 英语 accost 最初指靠到船或人的旁边。

items.en: Modern usage narrows it to speaking first, usually unwanted.
items.cn: 现代用法收窄为主动开口，且通常不受欢迎。

note.en: The first group gathers the participle and the related coast word; the second gathers verbs for approaching people.
note.cn: 第一组收分词与相关 coast 词；第二组收表示接近他人的动词。

entries.definition: The past participle, often used in news reports.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，常见于新闻报道。

entries.definition: The land beside the sea, from the Latin word for side.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海岸」，来自拉丁语「侧边」一词。

entries.definition: The present participle, as in accosting passers-by.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，如 accosting passers-by。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to come near someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接近」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to stop someone and force a conversation.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拦住某人硬要交谈」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to stop someone on their way.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「半路拦阻」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to trouble someone repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「反复骚扰」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'to the side' origin and the street scenes; the abstract hooks picture someone stepping into your path.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「到旁边」来源与街头场景；抽象记忆点想象有人横跨一步挡在你路上。

normal.en: Accost is 'to the side': Latin costa means rib or side.
normal.cn: accost 是「到旁边」：拉丁语 costa 意为肋骨、侧边。

normal.en: It usually implies an unwanted approach.
normal.cn: 这个词通常暗示不受欢迎的接近。

normal.en: Reporters accost ministers; touts accost tourists.
normal.cn: 记者拦住部长；拉客者缠住游客。

normal.en: The spelling has one c and double s.
normal.cn: 拼写为一个 c、双 s。

normal.en: Coast is a distant relative from the same side root.
normal.cn: coast 是同出「侧边」词根的远亲。

abstract.en: Picture a man stepping into the path of a traveller.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人横跨一步挡在旅客路上。

abstract.en: Picture a tout following a family down the street.
abstract.cn: 想象拉客者跟着一家人走过整条街。

abstract.en: Picture a microphone pushed toward a minister at the door.
abstract.cn: 想象话筒在门口被推到部长面前。

examples.en: She was accosted by a stranger asking for money.
examples.cn: 她被一名讨钱的陌生人拦住了。

examples.en: Journalists accosted the coach after the match.
examples.cn: 赛后记者们围住了教练。

examples.en: Do not accost visitors at the gate of the site.
examples.cn: 不要在工地门口纠缠来访者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿科斯特」——横跨一步站到你旁边开口，就是拦人搭话。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ costa（侧边）→ accostare（走到旁边）；核心义是「靠到别人身侧开口」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a bold unwanted approach, to repeated soliciting on the street.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从冒失而不受欢迎的接近，走到街头反复拉客乞讨。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone stepping sideways into your path
core.cn: 核心意象：有人横跨一步挡在你面前

branches.en: A person moving up to you and speaking first.
branches.cn: 走近并先开口的人。

branches.en: Repeated approaches that demand something.
branches.cn: 反复接近并提出要求。

branches.en: The physical approach is shared by both senses.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享同一个物理接近。

branches.en: Courtesy turns to nuisance when the approach repeats.
branches.cn: 接近一旦反复，礼貌就变成烦扰。

branches.en: The same verb covers a journalist and a tout.
branches.cn: 同一个动词覆盖记者与拉客者。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin prefix ad- with the side root cost-, and its family adds a participle form.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与「侧边」词根 cost- 结合，词族另加分词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin costa and accostare are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the noun and the verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 costa 与 accostare 是直接祖先，因此拉丁条目记录名词与动词。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「被拦住的」
名词化分词，义为「拦截行为」

definition_zh: 会计；会计师；报账人（古义）
definition_en: a person who keeps or inspects financial records, especially as a profession
core_image: 一个人把成堆的单据按规则排进格子，最后算出总数
scene: 年末审计前，财务室整夜亮着灯，会计逐张核对发票与入库单。The accountant found two invoices that had never been paid.
sceneCN: 这里 accountant 是「会计、会计师」（第 1 个义项：负责保存或核查财务记录的人）；句意为会计发现有两张发票从未付款。

derivatives.zh: 由本词词干加名词后缀构成，义为「会计业」
同源名词，义为「会计；记账」
同源形容词，义为「负有责任的」

senses.title: A keeper of financial records
senses.definition: a person whose job is to record money received and paid
senses.definitionCN: 职业上记录收入与支出的人
senses.example: The accountant enters every sale in the ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 会计把每笔销售记入账簿。
senses.why: The -ant ending marks the person who performs the reckoning, so the accountant is literally the one who accounts.
senses.whyCN: -ant 后缀标记执行该动作的人，因此 accountant 字面上就是「做结算的人」。

senses.title: A qualified financial professional
senses.definition: a trained professional who audits, advises, and certifies accounts
senses.definitionCN: 经训练、从事审计、咨询与账目鉴证的专业人士
senses.example: Only a registered accountant may sign the audit report.
senses.exampleCN: 只有注册会计师才能签署审计报告。
senses.why: As accounting became regulated, the everyday recorder turned into a licensed expert whose signature carries legal weight.
senses.whyCN: 随着会计业受监管，日常记账者变成持证专家，其签名具有法律效力。

senses.title: One who reports or answers
senses.definition: in older use, a person who gives an account of something
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法中，对某事作出陈述的人
senses.example: The steward was called the accountant of the household's stores.
senses.exampleCN: 管家被称为家中仓物的报账者。
senses.why: Before finance narrowed the word, any person who 'rendered an account' could be called an accountant.
senses.whyCN: 在金融义收窄之前，任何「报出账目」的人都可以叫 accountant。

intro.en: Accountant is the Latin-derived agent noun of account, formed with the -ant ending for a person who acts.
intro.cn: accountant 是 account 的拉丁语式施动名词，以 -ant 后缀指执行动作的人。

items.en: putare meant 'to reckon', the root of account.
items.cn: putare 意为「计算」，是 account 的词根。

items.en: computare meant 'to sum up together'.
items.cn: computare 意为「合计」。

items.en: aconter meant 'to recount or give an account'.
items.cn: aconter 意为「叙述、报账」。

items.en: The present participle acontant named one who accounts.
items.cn: 现在分词 acontant 指报账之人。

items.en: English accountant first meant a person who reports or explains.
items.cn: 英语 accountant 最初指作报告或解释的人。

items.en: Modern usage fixes the word in finance and auditing.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词固定在财务与审计领域。

note.en: The first group gathers the profession and practice nouns plus the responsibility adjective; the second gathers finance job words.
note.cn: 第一组收职业名词、工作名词与责任形容词；第二组收金融职位词。

entries.definition: The profession or practice of accounting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计业」。

entries.definition: The activity or system of keeping financial records.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计；记账」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning required to explain and answer for actions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负有责任的」。

entries.definition: The record or the act of reckoning behind the job.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「账户；账目」，该职业所依据的记录或计算。

entries.definition: A person who records daily financial transactions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「簿记员」，记录日常财务交易者。

entries.definition: A person who officially checks accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审计员」，正式核查账目者。

entries.definition: An officer who manages an organisation's money.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「财务主管」，管理组织资金者。

entries.definition: A senior finance officer in a company.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「财务总监」，公司高级财务主管。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -ant person rule and the audit scene; the abstract hooks picture a desk of receipts sorted into squares.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 -ant 指人规则与审计场景；抽象记忆点想象桌上单据被分进格子。

normal.en: Accountant is account plus -ant, the person who does the reckoning.
normal.cn: accountant 是 account 加 -ant，做结算的那个人。

normal.en: Chartered accountant is the British professional title.
normal.cn: chartered accountant 是英式专业头衔。

normal.en: The profession is accountancy, the activity accounting.
normal.cn: 职业是 accountancy，活动是 accounting。

normal.en: In American English certified public accountant is the standard title.
normal.cn: 美式英语中标准头衔是 certified public accountant。

normal.en: Accountable is the adjective, meaning answerable.
normal.cn: 形容词是 accountable，意为需作出交代。

abstract.en: Picture a desk covered in receipts sorted into labelled trays.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上单据被分进贴标签的托盘。

abstract.en: Picture a signature at the bottom of an audit report.
abstract.cn: 想象审计报告底部的签名。

abstract.en: Picture a steward reading out the household stores.
abstract.cn: 想象管家逐一报出家中仓物。

examples.en: Their accountant advised them to delay the purchase.
examples.cn: 他们的会计建议他们推迟采购。

examples.en: A chartered accountant must sign the annual accounts.
examples.cn: 年度账目须由特许会计师签署。

examples.en: The accountant reconciled the two sets of records.
examples.cn: 会计核对了这两套记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康特恩特」——把单据一张张算清的人，就是会计。

root: account（结算）+ -ant（执行者）；核心义是「以算账为职业的人」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the everyday recorder, to the licensed professional, to the older sense of anyone who reports.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从日常记账者，走到持证专业人士，再到旧有的「任何陈述者」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: receipts sorted into labelled trays at month's end
core.cn: 核心意象：月末单据被分进贴标签的托盘

branches.en: The employee who records every payment.
branches.cn: 记录每笔款项的雇员。

branches.en: The certified expert whose signature carries weight.
branches.cn: 签名具有效力的持证专家。

branches.en: The old sense of a person giving a report.
branches.cn: 旧有的「作出陈述者」义。

branches.en: The same job spans routine entries and formal certification.
branches.cn: 同一职业横跨日常记账与正式鉴证。

branches.en: Reporting and reckoning were once the same act.
branches.cn: 报告与结算曾是同一个动作。

intro.en: The word is the -ant person form of the reckoning verb, and its family adds the profession and activity nouns.
intro.cn: 这个词是「结算」动词的 -ant 人物形式，词族另加职业与活动名词。

latinIntro.en: French acontant, the present participle of aconter, is the immediate model, and computare is the Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 法语 acontant（aconter 的现在分词）是直接范型，computare 是拉丁语词根。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「会计业」
名词，义为「会计；记账」

definition_zh: 装备；配备（尤指军装军械）
definition_en: to equip or dress someone, especially a soldier, with the needed gear
core_image: 军械库前的配装台：一件件扣上腰带与弹药盒
scene: 黎明前的新兵列队，军士逐件为他扣上装具，直到镜中的人像样起来。The quartermaster will accouter the recruits before drill.
sceneCN: 这里 accouter 是「装备、配备」（第 1 个义项：给军人配齐装具）；句意为军需官将在操练前为新兵配装。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「装具；服饰装备」
由本词加过去分词后缀构成（英式拼写 accoutred），义为「配备装具的」

senses.title: To equip a soldier with gear
senses.definition: to provide someone, especially a soldier, with weapons, armour, and clothing
senses.definitionCN: 给某人（尤指军人）配发武器、盔甲与服装
senses.example: The armoury accoutered each guard before his watch began.
senses.exampleCN: 军械库在每名卫兵上岗前为其配装。
senses.why: The French source meant to sew onto a garment, and outfitting a soldier is adding one piece of gear after another to the body.
senses.whyCN: 法语原义是缝到衣服上；为士兵配装正是把一件件装具「缀」到身体上。

senses.title: To dress in a distinctive way
senses.definition: to clothe or adorn someone in a particular, often elaborate, style
senses.definitionCN: 以某种特定且常显考究的方式为某人着装打扮
senses.example: Guards were accoutered in ceremonial red and gold.
senses.exampleCN: 卫兵们被装点在仪式化的红金制服中。
senses.why: If a soldier can be covered with equipment, a courtier can be covered with finery; the same verb serves both.
senses.whyCN: 士兵可以被装具覆盖，廷臣也可以被华服覆盖；同一个动词兼顾两者。

intro.en: Accouter comes from Old French accoutrer, perhaps from cousture 'sewing', with earlier parts uncertain.
intro.cn: accouter 来自古法语 accoutrer，可能源于 cousture（缝纫），更早的成分来源不确定。

items.en: consuere meant to sew together, a likely ancestor via reconstruction.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语 consuere（缝合）可能是其重构的源头。

items.en: cousture meant a seam or sewing.
items.cn: 古法语 cousture 意为针脚、缝纫。

items.en: accoutrer meant to sew on, then to dress someone up.
items.cn: 古法语 accoutrer 意为缝上，后指为人装扮。

items.en: English accoutre first served military outfitting.
items.cn: 英语 accoutre 最初用于军队配装。

items.en: American spelling accouter and British accoutre coexist.
items.cn: 美式拼写 accouter 与英式 accoutre 并存。

note.en: The first group gathers the sewing-root family and spelling variants; the second gathers words for equipping.
note.cn: 第一组收缝纫词根词族与拼写变体；第二组收表示装备的词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的英式拼写。

entries.definition: The gear itself, as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，指装具本身。

entries.definition: High fashion sewing, from the same French sewing word.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指高级定制缝纫。

entries.definition: To supply with what is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「配备所需之物」。

entries.definition: To provide a full set of gear.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「配齐全套装备」。

entries.definition: To dress in fine or ordered clothes.
entries.definitionCN: 文学化动词，义为「盛装装扮」。

entries.definition: To clothe, especially finely.
entries.definitionCN: 正式动词，义为「着装；盛饰」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the sewing story and the spelling twins; the abstract hooks picture the armoury table.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用缝纫典故与拼写孪生词；抽象记忆点想象军械库的配装台。

normal.en: The French source meant to sew onto a garment.
normal.cn: 法语原义是缝到衣服上。

normal.en: Couture, high sewing, shares the same sewing root.
normal.cn: couture（高级缝纫）共享同一缝纫词根。

normal.en: British spelling drops the extra e-r: accoutre.
normal.cn: 英式拼写少一个 e-r：accoutre。

normal.en: The noun accouterment means the gear itself.
normal.cn: 名词 accouterment 指装具本身。

normal.en: Military contexts keep the word alive today.
normal.cn: 军事语境让这个词沿用至今。

abstract.en: Picture a sergeant buckling straps on a recruit, one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象军士长为新兵逐一扣上背带。

abstract.en: Picture a tailor sewing buckles straight onto a uniform.
abstract.cn: 想象裁缝把扣环直接缝上制服。

abstract.en: Picture a knight shining head to toe before the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象骑士在城门前从头到脚全副武装。

examples.en: The museum accoutered the mannequin with a genuine cavalry kit.
examples.cn: 博物馆为人体模型配上了真正的骑兵装具。

examples.en: Pages were accoutered in silk before the coronation.
examples.cn: 加冕礼前，侍从们被装点在丝绸之中。

examples.en: Historians study how seventeenth-century armies accoutered their foot soldiers.
examples.cn: 历史学家研究十七世纪的军队如何为步兵配装。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿库特」——把装备「库」里的一件件「特」快配上身。

root: 一般认为源自拉丁语 consuere（缝合）→ 古法语 cousture（缝）→ accoutrer（缝上；装扮）→ 英语 accouter（配装）

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from military outfitting piece by piece, to dressing in a distinctive style.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从逐件配发军装军械，扩展到以特定风格盛装打扮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fastening one piece of gear onto a body
core.cn: 核心意象：把一件件装具「缀」上身体

branches.en: Gear attached to a soldier until ready.
branches.cn: 装具一件件上身，直至战备。

branches.en: Finery attached for show instead of war.
branches.cn: 为仪态而非战斗披挂的华服。

branches.en: Both senses share the sewing-on picture.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享「缝上、缀上」的画面。

branches.en: The verb implies completeness of the kit.
branches.cn: 该动词暗示装具的齐全。

branches.en: Ceremony and parade keep the elaborate sense alive.
branches.cn: 仪式与阅兵保留着考究装扮的义项。

intro.en: The word joins a toward-prefix with the sewing stem and a verb ending; the family adds a gear noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由「向」前缀、「缝纫」词干与动词结尾组成；词族另派生装具名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin consuere is a reconstructed ancestor, so the Latin entry is marked as likely.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 consuere 是重构的祖先，拉丁条目按「可能来源」标注。
